# Vancouver Daily News
> **Sixty-four votes flip Burnaby South-Metrotown to the Conservatives, lifting their majority to sixty-four seats.**

**What You Need to Know:** Sixty-four votes have flipped Burnaby South-Metrotown from NDP incumbent Paul Choi to Conservative David Xie, taking the incoming Conservative majority to 64 of 93 seats. A 78-year-old woman has died after being struck at Dunbar Street and West 34th Avenue, Vancouver’s 13th fatal traffic collision this year, and police say no charges have been laid. In Chilliwack, a 55-year-old man has been charged with second-degree murder in the death of a 52-year-old woman.

### Top Stories
**Recount flips squeaker election night win for NDP in Burnaby South-Metrotown to Conservatives: Vancouver Sun**
Elections B.C. completed the final count Sunday and declared Conservative David Xie the winner in Burnaby South-Metrotown, 64 votes ahead of NDP incumbent Paul Choi, who had won the seat in 2024. Choi’s election-night lead was 66 ballots, a 0.5 per cent margin; the final margin was 0.43 per cent, just enough to avoid an automatic judicial review, an Elections B.C. spokeswoman said. The Vancouver Sun reported the flip takes the incoming majority to 64 of 93 seats, and that under premier-designate Lorne Doerkson the Conservatives will control almost 70 per cent of the next legislature. Two other races kept their election-night winners but go to judicial review because each margin was under 0.2 per cent of the riding’s eligible votes. In Ladysmith-Oceanside, NDP Stephanie Higginson’s lead grew from 13 votes on election night to 50 in the final count. In Kelowna Centre, a partial recount of one polling station narrowed Conservative Kristina Loewen’s lead over NDP Loyal Wooldridge from 137 votes to 43. The final count added mail-in ballots, absentee ballots and telephone-assisted votes. Xie did not immediately return a request for comment. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/elections-bc-recount-flips-squeaker-election-night-win-for-ndp-in-burnaby-south-metrotown-to-conservatives) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/vaughn-palmer-conservatives-flip-another-seat-final-elections-bc-tally) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/david-xie-bc-conservative-elected-9.7415041?cmp=rss)

**Orange warnings raised over next B.C. deluge, as second death linked to wild weather: North Shore News**
Power is back for most B.C. Hydro customers ahead of the next round, the Vancouver Sun reported, with another strong series of storms expected from Tuesday through Thursday. North Shore News reported forecasters are escalating rainfall warnings in southwest British Columbia, and that some areas could receive more than 250 millimetres. That report also linked a second death to the wild weather. CBC reported the third storm in the series is heading for the coast after a weekend that knocked out power to thousands, triggered evacuations and left one person dead. In Prince George, CBC reported Friday night’s windstorm is still being cleaned up, and B.C. Hydro said power there may not be fully restored until Tuesday. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/orange-warnings-raised-over-next-bc-deluge-as-second-death-linked-to-wild-weather-12994785) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-wind-storm-november-2026-power-restored-new-weather-alert) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/rain-winds-storm-bc-9.7414681?cmp=rss) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/prince-george-windstorm-power-trees-down-9.7415230?cmp=rss)

**78-year-old pedestrian dies after being struck during heavy rainstorm: Vancouver Police Department**
A 78-year-old woman died after a Lexus sedan struck her while she crossed Dunbar Street in an unmarked crosswalk at West 34th Avenue. Vancouver police said the collision was about 11 a.m. on November 6, witnesses described heavy rain, the driver remained and cooperated, and the woman died the next day at Vancouver General Hospital. Sergeant Adam Donaldson said the investigation is ongoing and no charges have been laid. Police said it was Vancouver’s 13th fatal traffic collision of the year. The department has launched Project Vigilance for the longer hours of darkness, with patrols at high-risk intersections and school zones through the winter solstice on December 21. Donaldson said the clocks are not turning back, so people need to be more aware of the darkness, and that officers will target speeding, distracted driving, impaired driving, jaywalking and lack of helmets. He also said a reflector clipped to a bag or clothing will help drivers see people dressed in black. Source: [vpd.ca](https://vpd.ca/news/2026/11/09/78-year-old-pedestrian-dies-after-being-struck-during-heavy-rainstorm/) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/death-vancouver-fatal-traffic-collision) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-police-e-scooter-death)

**Chilliwack man, 55, charged with 2nd-degree murder of woman: Surrey Now-Leader**
Kristopher John Hayward, 55, has been charged with second-degree murder after a 52-year-old woman was found dead Friday, November 6. Chilliwack RCMP said they were called at about 8:09 p.m. to a residence in the 46000 block of Mellard Avenue and found a woman who was pronounced dead at the scene. The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team took over, working with Chilliwack RCMP, the Integrated Forensic Identification Service and the BC Coroners Service. The BC Prosecution Service approved the charge the next day, and IHIT announced it Monday. Police did not identify the woman. Investigators believe Hayward and the woman knew each other and that the incident was not random. Sergeant Freda Fong of IHIT said charges met the approval standard within 24 hours of the team deploying, and that work continues with the family and the prosecution. Hayward’s next court appearance is Tuesday, November 10. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/09/chilliwack-man-55-charged-with-2nd-degree-murder-of-woman/)

### City & Province
**Vandalism prompts all-day closure of Langley elementary school: Vancouver Sun**
Langley police are investigating vandalism discovered inside Noel Booth Elementary in the Brookswood community of Langley Township, and the school was closed to students for the full day Monday. The Langley school district first posted a 10 a.m. late start “due to vandalism and necessary cleanup,” then updated the post around 9 a.m. to say the school would be closed all day and asked families to pick up students. Spokesperson Joanne Abshire confirmed the closure, said the vandalism was found inside the school, and said Langley RCMP are investigating. She said the district would share an update with families later Monday. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/langley-police-investigating-after-vandalism-prompts-all-day-school-closure)

**Man charged after loaded handgun found during traffic stop: CityNews Vancouver**
An 18-year-old Surrey resident, Paramveer Singh Deol, has been charged after Surrey police said they stopped a white Porsche whose driver was accelerating and went through a red light. With Project Assurance members, officers stopped the vehicle, identified and arrested the driver, and found a loaded firearm in a search after the arrest. CityNews reported the charges include failing to stop for police, occupying a vehicle with a firearm inside, possession of a loaded firearm without a licence, and careless transport of a firearm, a 9mm pistol. Deol remains in custody awaiting a bail hearing, the Surrey Police Service said. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/11/09/surrey-man-charged-loaded-handgun-traffic-stop/)

**Kelowna MP Stephen Fuhr speaks on federal budget to end homelessness: Surrey Now-Leader**
The federal government tabled its 2027 budget on November 5, with almost $30 billion aimed at eliminating homelessness within 10 years and $15 billion to triple annual non-market housing starts to 24,000. Kelowna MP Stephen Fuhr, Secretary of State for Defence Procurement, spoke at Pleasantvale II, a mix of market and non-market units housing people evacuated from UBC Okanagan’s Hadgraft Wilson building. He said the building came together with federal, provincial and municipal support and the Society of Hope, and that communities can apply for the new funding. Fuhr said Kelowna “always meets the terms and conditions, gets projects out of the ground and they do it quickly,” and he called the $45 billion budgeted to address homelessness “aggressive, but it’s necessary.” He said he is looking forward to meeting premier-elect Lorne Doerkson. Black Press has asked Kelowna Mayor Tom Dyas whether the city plans to use the federal funding. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/09/kelowna-mp-stephen-fuhr-speaks-on-federal-budget-to-end-homelessness/)

**Richmond autism network gets funding for independence programs: Richmond News**
Richmond’s autism network has funding for independence programs, and Pacific Blue Cross members can vote daily until November 24 to direct an extra $50,000. Source: [richmond-news.com](https://www.richmond-news.com/local-news/richmond-bc-autism-network-gets-pacific-blue-cross-funding-for-independence-programs-12998737)

### The Closer Look
**Vancouver Whitecaps aren't the only Canadian MLS team in danger of relocating to United States: Daily Hive Vancouver**
The Vancouver Whitecaps are for sale and at risk of a move to the United States, and Daily Hive Vancouver reports they are no longer the only Canadian Major League Soccer club in that position. On Monday, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that club is up for sale as well. He told reporters, “If the club doesn’t find a local buyer and I get an offer where the club needs to be relocated, then I have no choice. That is the decision I will take.” He also said, “I will not discount the club to the point of just giving it away,” that he loves the club and would love it to stay, and that selling to someone who cannot keep it there would not be doing anyone a favour.

The Whitecaps have been for sale for nearly two years and have yet to find a buyer who wants to keep the franchise in Vancouver. That uncertainty has run through the two most successful seasons the club has had in MLS. The Whitecaps reached the MLS Cup Final last year. This season they set a franchise record of 64 points, with a Western Conference-leading record of 19 wins, 8 losses and 7 draws.

Montreal’s season went the other way. The club finished with an MLS-worst record of 6 wins, 20 losses and 8 draws. Daily Hive described a stadium problem that does not match Vancouver’s: MLS is moving to a winter schedule, and Montreal’s outdoor stadium is not suitable for more matches on that calendar. The Whitecaps play at BC Place, which has a retractable roof, so winter weather is not the same obstacle. The problem in Vancouver, the outlet reported, appears to be the current business model.

Of Canada’s three MLS clubs, Toronto FC appears safe for now. The same report set the two sales against earlier departures from Canadian cities: the Quebec Nordiques moved to Colorado in 1995, the Winnipeg Jets left for Phoenix in 1996, the Vancouver Grizzlies left for Memphis in 2001, and the Montreal Expos relocated to Washington, D.C., in 2004. For people who follow the Whitecaps, the new dated fact is Saputo’s Monday statement that a Canadian owner will accept a move if that is what a sale requires, while Vancouver’s own sale, nearly two years on, still has no buyer committed to keeping the team here. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/whitecaps-arent-only-canadian-mls-team-danger-relocating)

### Also Today
**Community-led search for missing Ma’amtagila Nation man amplifies, family says resources still needed: CBC British Columbia**
A family-led search has intensified for a missing Ma’amtagila Nation father last seen canoeing in ocean waters 85 kilometres northwest of Campbell River. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/indigenous/james-smith-missing-maamtagila-nation-9.7415743?cmp=rss)

A federal secretary of state says relief is on its way for Richmond households, touting a grocery-benefit boost and housing money, while Conservatives criticize added debt. One trustee seat was still empty at the Surrey School Board’s inaugural meeting. Source: [pentictonherald.ca](https://www.pentictonherald.ca/spare_news/article_c9016518-f13a-5bec-97f7-ade29c83d088.html)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Surrey council is asked today to approve all fifteen of Doug McCallum's campaign promises at once.**

**What You Need to Know:** Surrey council is asked today to approve all fifteen of Doug McCallum's campaign promises at once. The vote is on the inaugural meeting agenda, and UBC political scientist Stewart Prest says the package reaches past what a city motion can settle on its own. Power crews are still working storm damage that could last into Tuesday, and a Seaspan drydock is back in the harbour after work overseas.

### Top Stories
**Surrey Mayor Doug McCallum calls for immediate action on all campaign promises: Vancouver Sun**
Surrey council is being asked to vote yes to all of newly elected mayor Doug McCallum's campaign promises at its inaugural meeting on Monday. McCallum, serving a fifth term after terms from 1996 to 2005 and 2018 to 2022, was re-elected with 31.8 per cent of the vote. He and the Safe Surrey Coalition won all but one seat on the nine-member council on a 15-point agenda. Items named for the vote include withdrawing the city from Metro Vancouver while maintaining core services, equipping the Surrey Police Service with a helicopter and drone fleet within three months, freezing property taxes, using city-owned land in Newton for a new women and children's hospital, building pools in Clayton Heights, Newton and Cloverdale, providing free swim lessons for children, protecting farm land, and promoting a SkyTrain expansion down King George Boulevard to Newton. At his inauguration address on Nov. 3, McCallum said, "The people of Surrey did not elect this council to study things. They elected us to get things done, and that work starts at our first meeting." UBC political scientist Stewart Prest said staff are normally asked to report back before council decides, and called the strategy unusual. Prest said, "This is extremely Doug McCallum," and, "I am concerned he is biting off too much too quickly with this approach." Prest said a helicopter and drone purchase alongside a property-tax freeze would require significant cuts elsewhere, and that Surrey cannot simply pass a motion to leave Metro Vancouver, which handles the region's drinking water, wastewater treatment, solid waste management and regional parks. Prest said a pullout, even if successful, would leave a significant hole in regional governance and real costs. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/surrey-mayor-doug-mccallum-calls-for-immediate-action-on-all-campaign-promises)

**B.C. Hydro power outages could stretch into Tuesday as crews continue to repair storm damage: CBC British Columbia**
B.C. Hydro says repairs after the weekend wind storm could stretch into Tuesday. As of 5 p.m. PCT Sunday, customers without power had fallen from roughly 135,000 overnight Saturday to about 30,000, the utility said. More than 8,000 of those remaining outages were in the Central Interior. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-hydro-outages-progress-made-9.7414525?cmp=rss)

**Massive Seaspan drydock returns from overseas upgrades: North Shore News**
Seaspan Careen is back in Vancouver harbour this week after upgrades in Indonesia. North Shore News reports the drydock will be back in its usual spot on the North Vancouver waterfront in February. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/massive-seaspan-drydock-returns-from-overseas-upgrades-12991492)

### City & Province
**Fatal grizzly attack triggers debate about B.C. hunting ban: Vancouver Sun**
As daily life resumes after a deadly grizzly bear attack on a mother and daughter in Bella Coola, the Vancouver Sun reports that calls to reopen B.C.'s grizzly bear hunt are growing louder. There were about 15,000 grizzly bears across B.C. in 2018, and some say updated numbers are needed. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/fatal-grizzly-attack-triggers-debate-about-bc-hunting-ban)

**Okanagan Falls swears in its first ever mayor and council: CBC British Columbia**
Okanagan Falls swore in its first mayor and council on Friday. Mayor Matt Taylor took the oath with councillors Amy Bydal, Eugene Dettling, Randy Ludwar and Allison Symons. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/okanagan-falls-swears-in-its-first-ever-mayor-and-council-9.7413475?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**B.C. soldier killed in CFB Wainwright fire found 'purpose, family' in military, mother says at Vancouver funeral: Vancouver Sun**
Private Aidan Goulding was honoured Sunday morning at a military armoury in Vancouver. Family, friends and colleagues filled the room for the 23-year-old, one of four men killed in a fire at CFB Wainwright. His mother, Sonia Monk, said he could always make anyone laugh. She called him fearless, sometimes more fearless than she would have preferred, and said he loved life and wanted to experience all of it. She thanked people for the outpouring of support in recent weeks and called him her bright light. She said she feels as if she is driving with one headlight: the road is still there and she will try to keep moving forward, but it will never be quite as bright.

Goulding had been on live-fire exercises at CFB Wainwright last month, training for potential deployment overseas, when a grass fire overtook soldiers. Global News reported that Alberta saw uncommonly strong winds that day. The fire killed Goulding, Sergeant Morgan Wong, Private Shaun Farrell and Private Hayden Lykkemark. Another 39 soldiers were taken to hospital at the time. Funerals for Wong and Farrell have been held in recent weeks. An investigation is ongoing, including into the grass fire.

Goulding served with the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, which was part of that training. Captain Jack O'Connell, his commander, called him an outgoing, confident, charismatic warrior. O'Connell said Goulding completed infantry training in July 2026 before being posted to the battalion, and that he often saw him on runs after work or going the extra mile. At Seaforth Armoury, Goulding's brother Wylder said the siblings got into all kinds of mischief when they were younger, from bike riding and tree climbing to skateboarding, often ending up hurt. Wylder called him his best friend, his worst enemy, his harshest critic and his fiercest competitor, and said Aidan went places, met people, had adventures and got into situations most people could not imagine. Monk said the family will continue with something always missing while the investigation goes on. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/funeral-held-pte-aidan-goulding-vancouver-cfb-wainwright-fire) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12141990/aidan-goulding-funeral-cfb-wainwright-fire/)

### Also Today
**1 dead after tree falls on 2 vehicles during second B.C. storm: Global BC**
One person is dead after a tree fell on two vehicles during British Columbia's second storm of the weekend, Global BC reports, as strong winds downed trees and left thousands without power, with more gusts expected. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12141788/bc-storms-power-outages-strong-winds/)

**Coquitlam clinic loses lawsuit against former employee who joined Port Moody competitor: Tri-Cities Dispatch**
A Coquitlam clinic has lost a lawsuit against a former employee who joined a competitor in Port Moody. Source: [tricitiesdispatch.com](https://tricitiesdispatch.com/three-step-fitness-employment-contract-lawsuit-song-coquitlam/)

**Kelowna firefighters shave heads to support cancer-stricken colleague: Surrey Now-Leader**
Kelowna firefighters shaved their heads to support a colleague who is ill with cancer. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/08/kelowna-firefighters-shave-heads-to-support-cancer-stricken-colleague/)

**Avis Blackbird shares journey from poetry to debut book: CityNews Vancouver**
Vancouver's Avis Blackbird, who used poetry as a teenager and later stepped away from writing as life intervened, is talking about the path to a debut book. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/11/08/blackbird-debut-poetry-book/)

**Edmonton Beat B.C. Twice in One Night: Elks Top the Lions, Then Fajardo Watches the Oilers Beat the Canucks: Culture Alberta**
The Edmonton Elks topped the B.C. Lions on the same night Cody Fajardo watched the Oilers play the Canucks. Source: [culturealberta.com](https://www.culturealberta.com/articles/edmonton-beat-bc-twice-in-one-night-elks-top-the-lions-then-fajardo-watches-the-oilers-beat-the-canu)

### Getting Around
A special weather statement is in effect for Vancouver and for Sea to Sky from Squamish to Whistler: people in or near those areas should watch for adverse weather and take safety precautions. On Highway 1, the stretch from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford is closed all day, every day, until December 31, with a detour and eastbound traffic shifted south of the median. Separate Highway 1 work from 216th Street to 264th Street and Highway 13 in Langley runs overnight, 9 p.m. to 7 a.m., through 7 a.m. Tuesday, with lanes closed both ways and the eastbound off-ramp at 232nd Street closed. Another Highway 1 work zone runs overnight until December 15, single lane both directions, with a 60 km/h limit, ending at 5:30 a.m. on weekdays and 7:30 a.m. on weekends. Highway 91A bridge maintenance continues until November 15, down to one lane each way from 9:30 p.m. to 5 a.m. on weeknights and until 9 a.m. on weekend mornings. Highway 7B bridge work is weekday daytime, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., with delays, two lanes each way, width limits, and commercial vehicles required to use both lanes. Vancouver was partly cloudy and 5.6 degrees this morning. Today turns cloudy with rain this afternoon, a high of 12, wind light except southeast 30 km/h near the water, then 10 to 15 millimetres tonight and a low of 7. Tuesday is rain, 10 to 20 millimetres, high 12, and a windy night with a low of 13. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**How to watch tonight's streaming-only Vancouver Canucks game: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Tonight's Vancouver Canucks game against the Philadelphia Flyers is not on the TV guide. It streams only on Sportsnet+ as Monday Night Hockey, with puck drop at 7:30 p.m. PCT at Rogers Arena. Former Canucks head coach Rick Tocchet is in with the Flyers. Sportsnet TV subscribers need an extra $12.99 a month for the stream. A Sportsnet+ subscription without TV is $34.99 a month or $269.99 a year. Rogers Xfinity TV customers who already have Sportsnet do not pay extra. This is the first of nine Canucks games streamed only on Sportsnet+ this season: November 9 against Philadelphia, November 16 against Utah, December 7 against Washington, December 14 against San Jose, December 21 against Utah, December 28 against Los Angeles, January 18 against Colorado, February 1 against Montreal, and March 29 against Los Angeles. Two further Canucks games this season are Wednesday-night exclusives on Prime Video and need that subscription as well. Sportsnet told Offside it is working with other Canadian distribution partners so TV subscribers have more ways to reach Sportsnet+ games. The Flyers are 4-10-5 and the Canucks are 3-15-1, seven points, and the Canucks are winless in their last five. Brock Boeser has 498 career points after a goal Saturday in Edmonton, with seven goals and nine assists for 16 points in 19 games. Two more points would make him the eighth player to 500 with the franchise. Elias Pettersson has four goals and 15 assists for 19 points in 19 games. Brendan Batchelor has the radio call on KiSS West Coast. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/how-to-watch-tonights-streaming-only-canucks-game) Source: [insidetherink.com](https://insidetherink.com/nhl-game-preview-philadelphia-flyers-at-vancouver-canucks-with-line-combinations-11-09-2026/) Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/canucks-return-to-rogers-arena-to-face-philadelphia-flyers-on-monday-night)

**Vancouver Rise bow out after loss to Montreal Roses in NSL semifinal series: CBC British Columbia**
The Montreal Roses are through to the Northern Super League final after beating the Vancouver Rise 5-2 over a two-game semifinal series. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/nsl-playoffs-montreal-roses-vancouver-rise-november-8-9.7412674?cmp=rss)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A 19-year-old woman is dead after an e-scooter hit a bus on Seymour Street.**

**What You Need to Know:** A 19-year-old woman is dead after an e-scooter and a transit bus collided on Seymour Street in Vancouver. Police say she and a man were riding the scooter northbound when they hit the side of a westbound bus head-on, and the Vancouver Sun reports neither rider was wearing a helmet. Wind warnings, Highway 10 in Surrey, and more storm systems are the other immediate problems for anyone moving around the South Coast this morning.

### Top Stories
**19-year-old woman killed in collision between e-scooter and transit bus in Vancouver: CBC British Columbia**
Police say a man and a woman were riding an e-scooter northbound on Seymour Street when they collided head-on with the side of a westbound transit bus. The woman, 19, was killed. The Vancouver Sun reports that neither the victim nor the man riding with her on the scooter was wearing a helmet. CBC's account is the collision itself: two people on one scooter, a transit bus travelling west, and a head-on strike into the side of that bus on Seymour. The Sun's added fact is the helmets. Neither outlet's copy in today's file names the bus route, the hour, or whether anyone else was hurt. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-e-scooter-fatality-bus-9.7413724?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/woman-hit-by-bus-killed-while-riding-e-scooter-in-vancouver)

**It's not over yet: B.C. Hydro warns of more storm systems on the way: Vancouver Sun**
After B.C. was hit by wet, windy weather on Friday, B.C. Hydro says to expect more challenging weather in the days ahead. The Vancouver Sun's headline puts it plainly: it is not over yet, and more storm systems are on the way. Global News reports that as storms continue, authorities are warning about high winds bringing more power outages and about the dangers of rising water levels, after what officials called minor flooding from the first of the season's storms. CBC reports that a round of blustery fall weather had already caused ferry cancellations and knocked out power to thousands, and that the South Coast appears set for another blast of wind. Fraser Valley Today reports more than 15,000 customers lacked power in Langley and Surrey on Saturday, and that Langley RCMP were responding to crashes caused by fallen trees. Farther north, CBC reports wind gusts up to 100 km/h in Prince George and the region on Friday night, with trees down on homes and, in one case, a traffic light gone from its location. The local picture this morning is the same system still moving through: outages already counted in the thousands in Langley and Surrey, ferries already cancelled in the earlier round, minor flooding already reported, and Hydro saying the next systems are still ahead. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/its-not-over-b-c-hydro-warns-of-storm-systems) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12141176/bc-storms-minor-flooding/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-south-coast-wind-warnings-9.7413548?cmp=rss)

**Whitecaps standing strong for Belal Halbouni in his cancer fight: Vancouver Sun**
The new fact is the contract. Centre back Belal Halbouni revealed Friday that he has been diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma, a cancer that affects white blood cells and is considered aggressive, though B.C. Cancer says treatment works well for most people. He is 26. He began treatment last week in his hometown of London, Ontario. He has not played since last fall, after a knee injury at the end of the playoff series against Los Angeles FC that needed surgical repair. He had been a key performer late in the season and in the playoffs while other Whitecaps defenders were hurt. The club and the player had hoped he would be back by now. His deal had been up at the end of this season. The Whitecaps offered a contract that does not stop at the end of the 2027 sprint season next June. It runs through the end of the 2027-28 season. Chief executive Axel Schuster told Postmedia the club does not know when Halbouni will be able to play again, and that doing the right thing for the player did not seem to have been in doubt. Schuster said, in the team's account: "As a club, we have made the decision to support Belal throughout this difficult process by providing him with stability, security, and peace of mind, while also giving him a positive goal to work toward, his return to the training field and to playing in MLS." He added, "We will be here for him every step of the way, and we look forward to welcoming him back when the time is right." Halbouni said in a statement released by the team: "I want to express my gratitude to Vancouver Whitecaps FC. The way this club has stood by me goes far beyond football, and it has reminded me what it truly means to be part of a family. I'm proud to represent this badge, grateful to call Vancouver home, and thankful for the light at the end of the tunnel that they give me." Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/sports/whitecaps-standing-strong-for-belal-halbouni-in-his-cancer-fight/wcm/8dd267f9-87ed-4b06-a9ab-df6973b37be9)

### City & Province
**$1.7M Vancouver home sells for half the price at tax auction: CBC British Columbia**
CBC reports a Vancouver home valued at $1.7 million sold for half that price at this year's City of Vancouver tax sale. The home was among more than 60 properties auctioned off. The sale was set off by owners who have not paid their taxes for three years in a row. Reserve prices, also called upset prices, were set at the amounts owed to the city. That is the mechanism in the copy: three missed years, a city auction, a floor equal to the tax debt, and at least one house whose assessed figure was $1.7 million changing hands at half that. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-tax-auction-affordable-homes-9.7410067?cmp=rss)

**'Absolutely' possible: Vancouver, Victoria mayors back Ottawa's bid to end homelessness: CBC British Columbia**
The mayors of Vancouver and Victoria are backing Ottawa's bid to end homelessness, CBC reports. The federal Liberal budget, delivered Thursday, set aside $11.2 billion over the next four years in a bid to end homelessness in the next 10 years. The local stake is that two B.C. mayors, including Vancouver's, have lined up behind that federal timetable and that dollar figure. The money is federal. The people the bid is aimed at live in the cities those mayors represent. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-reaction-federal-homelessness-plan-9.7412841?cmp=rss)

### Getting Around
Highway 10 in Surrey is closed because a tree is on the road, from 394 metres east of 180 Street to 398 metres west of 182 Street. DriveBC's last update was 4:56 a.m. Pacific time, with a next update listed for 7:00 a.m. On Highway 1 through the Langley district, road construction runs from 216th Street to 264th Street, also signed as Highway 13, from 9:00 p.m. Friday, November 6, until 7:00 a.m. Tuesday, November 10. The overnight window is 9:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. the next day, Monday and Friday through Sunday, with lane closures in both directions. The eastbound off-ramp at 232nd Street is closed for installation of a sign bridge and for paving. End times will vary. A separate Highway 1 closure runs from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford, all day, every day, from October 30 until 12:00 a.m. on December 31, with a detour in effect and eastbound traffic shifted south of the median. Highway 91A is reduced to one lane each direction for bridge maintenance until Sunday, November 15. Weekend work runs from 9:30 p.m. to 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. Crews are on the bridge and a speed-limit reduction is in effect. Highway 7B has bridge construction on weekdays from 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., two lanes each direction, width restrictions in effect, commercial vehicles required to use both lanes, and oversized loads requiring a permit. That work began December 1, 2025. Another Highway 1 construction window runs until Tuesday, December 15, overnight from 9:00 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. on weekdays and until 7:30 a.m. on weekends, with a 60 km/h speed limit and single-lane traffic in both directions. Environment Canada has a yellow wind warning for Vancouver, issued at 5:06 a.m. Pacific time Sunday, telling people in or near the area to watch for adverse weather and take safety precautions. Special weather statements are also up for the Coquihalla from Hope to Merritt, the Coquihalla from Merritt to Kamloops, and the Okanagan Connector from Merritt to Kelowna, each issued at 4:04 a.m. Current conditions in Vancouver are cloudy and 11.5 degrees. Sunday: a few showers ending this morning, then a mix of sun and cloud with a 30 percent chance of showers, a risk of thunderstorms early this morning, and southwest wind at 40 km/h gusting to 60, except gusting to 90 at times early, becoming southwest 20 gusting to 50 this morning and then light. Sunday night is partly cloudy with a low of plus 4. Monday is a mix of sun and cloud, becoming cloudy near noon, then rain, with an east wind of 20 km/h early in the afternoon, a high of 11, and a UV index of 1, or low. Monday night brings periods of rain and a low of 10. Tuesday is rain, windy, with a high of 12. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Draisaitl nets 2 as Edmonton Oilers dump Vancouver Canucks 4-2: Surrey Now-Leader**
The Oilers beat the Canucks 4-2 on Saturday at Rogers Place. Leon Draisaitl scored twice and is at 16 goals. Mattias Ekholm and Jason Dickinson also scored. Connor McDavid added three assists. Devon Levi made 20 saves in his return from injury. Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored for Vancouver. Leevi Merilainen stopped 26 of 29 shots. The Canucks are 3-15-1. They have lost five straight and 15 of their last 16. The Oilers are 12-3-3, and Global News reports they are 10-0-2 this season when they score first. They snapped a two-game losing skid. Edmonton opened the scoring 9:14 into the first, Ekholm one-timing a pass from McDavid from the right circle for his third goal of the year. Vancouver tied it with nine seconds left in the period, Sasson tipping a Jamie Oleksiak point shot, his fifth of the season, with Guillaume Brisebois also on the play. Shots after one were 12-4 for Edmonton. The second period was scoreless. Shots after 40 minutes were 21-10 for the Oilers. Dickinson made it 2-1 forty-nine seconds into the third, his second goal of the season, on a rebound off a Ty Emberson shot. Draisaitl made it 3-1 on the power play at the four-minute mark, another McDavid setup, his 15th of the season, with Evan Bouchard also assisting. Vancouver pulled Merilainen with four minutes left. Boeser redirected a Filip Hronek point shot with 2:35 left, his seventh, with Elias Pettersson also credited. With the goalie still on the bench, McDavid fed Draisaitl for an empty-netter with 45 seconds left. Global News reports McDavid's season-opening points and assists streak is now 18 games, matching Adam Oates for the second-longest assist streak in NHL history, behind only Wayne Gretzky's 23 games in 1990-91. McDavid leads the league with 10 goals, 37 assists and 47 points, and he is the sixth player in NHL history with a season-opening 18-game point streak. Coach Manny Malhotra said there were positives in the first two periods, that the attention to detail was there, and that the team had a chance to win going into the third. He said momentary lapses, missed assignments and a missed puck battle add up against a team as high-powered as Edmonton. Winger Jake DeBrusk called it a response to Thursday's loss in Winnipeg and said the record is 15 losses out of 16. Centre Max Sasson said the breakouts looked cleaner and that the team used the middle of the ice better for two periods. The Canucks host the Philadelphia Flyers on Monday at 7:30 p.m. at Rogers Arena. The Oilers host the New York Rangers on Monday. Surrey Now-Leader notes Vancouver is 116-129-19-15 all-time against Edmonton, and that defenceman Tom Willander missed a third straight game with a lower-body injury. Edmonton Elks quarterback Cody Fajardo, who earlier Saturday led his team to a Western Final win over the B.C. Lions, was at Rogers Place. The Edmonton Journal reports that football win came in front of 40,000 at Commonwealth Stadium and sent the Elks to the Grey Cup. On the hockey side, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins left after a puck hit the side of his face on a Ryan Shea dump-in midway through the first. He had played 6 minutes 38 seconds, after missing the first nine games and then putting up 11 points in eight. Oilers coach Mike Babcock said he does not think Nugent-Hopkins will miss time. Babcock said the first worry was a broken jaw, that medical staff assessed him, and that he seemed to be doing OK in the hallway. Babcock also said he would have liked a 6-0 win, and that a closer game was better because Vancouver pushed back and Edmonton had to stick to doing it right to get to a 3-1 lead. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/07/draisaitl-nets-2-as-edmonton-oilers-dump-vancouver-canucks-4-2/) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12141670/draisaitl-powers-oilers-past-canucks/) Source: [sportsnet.ca](https://www.sportsnet.ca/nhl/article/canucks-match-effort-by-high-powered-oilers-but-crumble-in-third-period/)

**CF Montréal 0 – Whitecaps FC 2: Sørensen sets MLS record: Indo-Canadian Voice**
The Whitecaps beat CF Montréal 2-0, and Indo-Canadian Voice reports that Sørensen set an MLS record. Source: [voiceonline.com](https://voiceonline.com/cf-montreal-0-whitecaps-fc-2-sorensen-sets-mls-record/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **LifeLabs must pay thirty-two thousand dollars after misgendering three patients in Vancouver and Burnaby.**

**What You Need to Know:** B.C.'s Human Rights Tribunal has ordered LifeLabs and a subsidiary to pay three transgender and non-binary people $32,000 for injury to their dignity after staff misgendered and outed them at service centres in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2019. Two men are now charged in a pair of Surrey shootings police have treated as extortion-related. Chilliwack has the first commercial poultry detection of avian flu in B.C. this season.

### Top Stories
**LifeLabs in B.C. ordered to pay $32K for misgendering transgender, non-binary patients: CBC British Columbia**
B.C.'s Human Rights Tribunal has ordered LifeLabs and a subsidiary to pay three transgender and non-binary people $32,000 for injury to their dignity. The tribunal found staff misgendered and outed them at service centres in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2019. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/lifelabs-human-rights-tribunal-bc-9.7412649?cmp=rss)

**Two men charged in 2025 Surrey extortion shootings: Vancouver Sun**
Pardeep Singh and Saveer Khan, both 22, are each charged with two counts of reckless discharge of a firearm in two October 2025 shootings. On Oct. 12, 2025, police responded to the 1300-block of 103A Avenue, where bullets were aimed at a home; a woman inside was shot in the torso, taken to hospital in critical condition, and later confirmed stable. On Oct. 16, Kap's Cafe, owned by Bollywood actor Kapil Sharma, was hit by gunfire — the third shooting at that restaurant in three months. The cafe was closed; two staff members were inside and neither was injured. The provincial extortion task force, the Combined Forces Special Enforcement Unit of B.C. and Surrey police arrested the two in Surrey on Nov. 1. Both remain in custody. Chief Supt. Duncan Pound of the B.C. RCMP said the charges followed a year of work, including judicial authorizations, search warrants and evidence analysis, and should be a message that police are working together on extortion-related violence. Since the beginning of the year, Surrey police have recorded 147 extortion threats, 21 of them involving shootings; in 2025, 49 of 133 extortion cases reported to police involved shootings. The City of Surrey has a $250,000 reward fund for tips that lead to charges. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/two-men-charged-in-2025-surrey-extortion-shootings)

**Chilliwack poultry facility reports 1st case of avian flu in B.C. this season: CBC British Columbia**
The Canadian Food Inspection Agency says the first avian flu detection in a commercial poultry flock in British Columbia this season was confirmed Friday in Chilliwack. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/chilliwack-poultry-avian-flu-season-9.7413285?cmp=rss)

**Seaspan makes largest order for heavy metal with Canadian steel mill: North Shore News**
North Vancouver shipbuilder Seaspan is paying $182 million for steel to build future icebreakers, its largest order of heavy metal with a Canadian steel mill. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/seaspan-makes-largest-order-for-heavy-metal-with-canadian-steel-mill-12986392)

### City & Province
**Landslide prompts evacuation order for Zeballos on Vancouver Island: CBC British Columbia**
Zeballos, a village of about 125 people on the northwest coast of Vancouver Island, is under a state of local emergency and an evacuation order because of flooding and landslide risks. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/zeballos-landslide-evacuation-order-9.7412402?cmp=rss)

**North Vancouver carbon monoxide poisoning prompts boiler safety order: North Shore News**
A lack of detectors in a North Vancouver apartment building let a gas leak go unnoticed earlier this year and sent six people to hospital, and the case has prompted a boiler safety order. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/north-vancouver-carbon-monoxide-poisoning-prompts-boiler-safety-order-12986496)

**Metro Vancouver appeal fails in multi-million-dollar land dispute in Langley: Aldergrove Star**
Metro Vancouver's appeal has failed in a multi-million-dollar land dispute in Langley. Source: [aldergrovestar.com](https://aldergrovestar.com/2026/11/07/metro-vancouver-appeal-fails-in-multi-million-dollar-land-dispute-in-langley/)

### The Closer Look
**U.S. Treasury sanctions Canadian firms connected to Ryan Wedding and Iran: Global BC**
The United States Treasury Department has sanctioned eight Canadian businesses for allegedly helping to evade sanctions on Iran's government. Bob Mackin reports that two of the money-services businesses are in North Vancouver. Global News says the Treasury acted with Fintrac, Canada's anti-money laundering watchdog, against money services businesses in British Columbia and Ontario.

Named companies based in Ontario and British Columbia include the Million Exchange, NIA Nations Currency, Farah Exchange, Darvish Exchange and several numbered companies. The department alleges several of the entities also worked with Ryan Wedding, the alleged drug kingpin and former Canadian Olympic snowboarder. It alleges he used several of these services to launder millions of dollars in drug money through digital assets before his arrest in January.

"Canada cannot be a safe haven for illicit financial facilitators that provide sanctions-evasion services to the Iranian regime and its proxies," U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a news release. "Treasury will pursue and disrupt the Iranian regime's financial channels anywhere in the world." Global News describes the sanctions as the latest U.S. move to clamp down on transactions evading sanctions as the United States continues its war with Iran.

Wedding was arrested in Mexico in January and taken to the United States to face drug trafficking, murder and attempted murder charges. He remains in federal custody awaiting two trials in March and October of next year. He represented Canada in a snowboarding slalom at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City, was later convicted in the United States of conspiracy to distribute cocaine, and was sentenced to prison in 2010. U.S. authorities allege that after his release he resumed drug trafficking. Eight people were also arrested in Canada a year ago as part of the U.S. investigation.

A Mexican judge was arrested this week on allegations that he accepted a $2-million bribe in exchange for granting bail to a man accused of acting as second-in-command to Wedding. The U.S. Department of Justice said Luis Benitez Alcantara is accused of unlawfully securing the release of Andrew Clark, a Canadian man alleged to have played a key role in a violent international drug trafficking ring. Wedding is alleged to have ordered the murders of several people, including a witness who could testify against him in a 2024 narcotics case. U.S. authorities have said he had been on the run for years.

For the North Vancouver businesses, the sanction is the change in force now: U.S. measures cover Canadian currency-exchange firms the Treasury accuses of serving the Iranian regime and, in several cases, Wedding. The next dates the coverage names are his trials in March and October of next year. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12140771/us-canada-sanctions-iran-ryan-wedding/) Source: [bobmackin.substack.com](https://bobmackin.substack.com/p/us-sanctions-two-north-vancouver)

The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra has appointed veteran arts executive Keith Cerny president and chief executive, replacing a retiring leader. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/entertainment/vancouver-symphony-orchestra-announces-new-ceo)

**Surrey Christmas Bureau's Toy Depot opens for donations of in-demand items, money: Peace Arch News**
The Surrey Christmas Bureau's Toy Depot is open for donations of in-demand items and money. Source: [peacearchnews.com](https://peacearchnews.com/2026/11/06/surrey-christmas-bureaus-toy-depot-opens-for-donations-of-in-demand-items-money/)

### Getting Around
A yellow wind warning is in effect for Vancouver, and special weather statements cover the Coquihalla from Hope to Merritt and Merritt to Kamloops, plus the Okanagan Connector from Merritt to Kelowna. On Highway 1 in Langley, overnight construction between 216th Street and 264th Street / Highway 13 runs from 9 p.m. to 7 a.m. through Tuesday morning, with lane closures both ways and the eastbound off-ramp at 232nd Street closed for sign-bridge installation and paving. A separate Highway 1 stretch from 256th Street to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford is closed around the clock until Dec. 31, with a detour and eastbound traffic shifted south of the median. Highway 99 night work in Delta, from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17, continues until Sunday, 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Monday to Saturday, with one lane open each way; Highway 91A bridge work reduces traffic to one lane each way on nights until Nov. 15; Highway 1 overnight work until Dec. 15 holds a 60 km/h limit and single-lane traffic both ways; Highway 7B weekday bridge work, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., keeps two lanes each way with width restrictions, and commercial vehicles must use both lanes. It is mostly cloudy and 9.9°C now. Saturday is cloudy, with a 30 percent chance of showers this morning and 70 percent late this afternoon, fog patches clearing, an east wind of 20 km/h gusting to 40, and a high of 14. Saturday night brings 15 to 25 mm of rain, a southeast wind of 30 km/h gusting to 50 and rising near midnight to 70 gusting to 90, and a low of 10. Sunday has showers ending early, then a mix of sun and cloud, 10 to 20 mm, a southwest wind of 50 km/h gusting to 70 becoming light near noon, and a high of 12; Sunday night is clear with a low of plus 5, and Monday has periods of rain and a high of 13. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Game Notes: Canucks at Oilers: NHL.com**
Tonight is the third of four Canucks-Oilers meetings this season: a 6-5 overtime win in Edmonton on Sept. 29, a 9-7 home loss on Oct. 1, tonight on the road, and March 21 at home. Vancouver is 116-128-19-15 all-time against Edmonton, 52-72-7-8 on the road, and 3-7-0 in the last 10. Brock Boeser has 37 points (20 goals, 17 assists) in 39 career games against Edmonton; Elias Pettersson has 26 points (10 goals, 16 assists) in 31. Kevin Lankinen is 2-6-0 with a 5.38 goals-against average and an .840 save percentage in nine career games against Edmonton. The Oilers host at Rogers Place, on Sportsnet at 9:00 p.m. MT. Edmonton is 11-3-3 and leads the NHL at 4.12 goals a game; Vancouver is 3-14-1 after four straight losses, its worst 18-game start, and sits at a league-worst 4.61 goals against. The teams combined for 27 goals in the first two meetings. The Canucks are 13-8-1-0 on Nov. 7 in franchise history and have never faced the Oilers on this date. Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/game-notes-canucks-at-oilers-110726) Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/oilers/news/preview-oilers-vs-canucks-11-06-26)

**Whitecaps' Halbouni says he has been diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma: TSN**
Vancouver Whitecaps centre back Belal Halbouni said Friday he has been diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma. The 26-year-old from London, Ont., began treatment in his hometown last week. Sporting director Axel Schuster said Halbouni and his family have the full support of the club, that Halbouni will step away to focus on treatment and recovery, and that the club will be there and looks forward to welcoming him back. The club also confirmed a contract extension through the 2027-28 season. Halbouni said he is grateful the club stood by him beyond football, proud to represent the badge, grateful to call Vancouver home, and thankful for the light at the end of the tunnel. He joined in February 2024 and has made 26 appearances. Vancouver (18-8-7, 61 points) leads the Western Conference and closes the regular season Saturday at CF Montreal. **Abbotsford Canucks' win streak stretches to 8: Surrey Now-Leader**
The Abbotsford Canucks have stretched their winning streak to eight. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/06/abbotsford-canucks-win-streak-stretches-to-8/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Three billion dollars is earmarked to replace the Massey Tunnel that Metro Vancouver commuters use.**

**What You Need to Know:** The 2026 federal budget sets aside three billion dollars for the Massey Tunnel replacement and millions for flood mitigation in British Columbia. Vancouver landlords were fined ninety thousand dollars after a house was split into twenty-one rooms, and Elections B.C. has started the provincial final count with about one hundred and fifty thousand mail-in ballots still to tally.

### Top Stories
**What the 2026 federal budget promises for B.C.: CBC British Columbia**
The 2026 federal budget earmarks several initiatives specifically for British Columbia, CBC British Columbia reports. That list includes three billion dollars for the Massey Tunnel replacement project and millions for flood mitigation. The tunnel money is the concrete local piece of a national budget: it is aimed at the Highway 99 crossing used by Metro Vancouver and Fraser River traffic. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/2026-federal-budget-british-columbia-bc-9.7411362?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver landlords fined $90K after dividing home into 21 rooms for 17 tenants: Global BC**
The Residential Tenancy Branch fined Vancouver landlords ninety thousand dollars after they divided a home into twenty-one rooms for seventeen tenants, Global BC reports. Following an investigation, the branch found the landlords did not maintain the rental property in compliance with health, safety and housing standards. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12138955/vancouver-landlords-fined-90k-dividing-home-21-rooms-17-tenants/)

**Elections B.C. begins final count after provincial election, some ridings still in balance: CBC British Columbia**
Elections B.C. has begun the final count after the provincial election, and CBC British Columbia reports that some ridings are still in balance. Elections B.C. said there are about one hundred and fifty thousand mail-in ballots to tally, in addition to absentee and assisted phone ballots that will be included in the final count. No outcome is settled by that tally until the count is finished. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/elections-bc-final-count-begins-9.7411300?cmp=rss)

**B.C. program for kids with long COVID scales back services after changes to MSP: CBC British Columbia**
The B.C. Centre for Long COVID reduced treatment options after changes to the Medical Services Plan came into force on November 1, CBC British Columbia reports. A Nanaimo teenager is among those losing access to support they say has changed their life. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/long-covid-clinic-msp-9.7406050?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**The life of Fry: A portrait of the artist and activist who became mayor of Vancouver: Vancouver Sun**
Pete Fry is Vancouver’s mayor-elect and the city’s first Green mayor, the Vancouver Sun reports, a week after an election-night party a few blocks from where a passerby stopped him on Burrard Street. Christina Modonese, a sixty-year resident of the West End, told him she had voted for another candidate and was hoping he would do well; he shook her hand and thanked her. Fry was born in Dublin in 1969 and the family immigrated to Canada when he was two, settling in Vancouver; he grew up in Dunbar. His mother, Hedy Fry, became a Liberal member of Parliament in 1993. The Consulate General of Ireland in Vancouver congratulated the city’s first Irish-born mayor since Robert Alexander Anderson, who was born in Armagh in 1856. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/pete-fry-profile)

**B.C. woman sentenced to 13 years in prison in sex trafficking case: Global BC**
Jennifer Lynn Stephens has been sentenced to thirteen years in prison in a sex trafficking case, Global BC reports. The human trafficking victims included several adults, as well as a thirteen-year-old girl who had already been the victim of sex trafficking. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12138820/jennifer-stephens-human-trafficking-sentence/)

### The Closer Look
**It can cost thousands to get rid of an old RV in B.C., so people are dumping them: Vancouver Sun**
On October 31, a travel trailer appeared overnight in a cornfield off a quiet country road in Abbotsford. Neighbours later remarked that someone had taken care to back it neatly into the field before driving away. The Vancouver Sun reports that abandoned recreational vehicles are showing up in fields, forests, rest areas and parks because disposing of an old RV in British Columbia is difficult and costly.

Phil Pires, a junk-removal expert who owns Big Phil’s Rubbish Removal and specializes in RV recycling, says people think the units have scrap value, but they do not. The only metal is the frame, and the whole unit has to be dismantled to reach it: sawing through siding and layers of insulation, separating Fiberglas from wood and upholstery, and draining the grey and black water tanks. Landfills may take some pieces, while recyclers take others. Tanks that once held septic waste have to be handled carefully, as do old fridges and appliances that might contain ammonia. Pires says that work is expensive. Disposal of a small camper, including the kind that fits on the back of a truck, typically runs about one thousand dollars. Large trailers can cost several thousand dollars. If the RV is worth fixing and he can find a buyer, he charges for removal, accepts legal ownership and then sells it for refurbishing. In other cases, owners balk. Some pay a company about two hundred dollars to take a unit away. Pires says if that seems too good to be true, it usually is. He recalled a woman in a Maple Ridge community Facebook group offering several hundred dollars to have an old boat removed. He gave her a quote; she did not call back. Several days later, a neighbour saw the boat abandoned on the side of the highway in Deroche. Police investigated. Pires said he does not think she was charged.

Abbotsford police Sergeant Paul Walker says illegal dumping is not typically a police matter. Officers may get involved if the vehicle is stolen, connected to a crime or presents a public safety risk. RVs have a VIN, but tracing it is complicated because people sometimes do not update the registration when they sell. Walker says that in most cases these abandoned RVs and vehicles are uninsured and, quite often, have been off insurance for many years, and that proving who dumped one is challenging.

Abbotsford is home to a large number of RVs, old and new, and several large dealerships. Until recently there were three RV encampments in highway rest areas and truck parking lots. At one time close to eighty old vehicles were in the camps, some abandoned before being occupied by people looking for shelter. The province closed the camps as construction on Highway 1 progressed. In a statement, the City of Abbotsford said bylaw officers responded to four reports of abandoned vehicles in the last year, including two RVs, a trailer and a boat. When the provincial government closed the camps, the city responded to three calls related to occupied RVs on city land and worked to connect the occupants with support services. Abandoned RVs have also been an issue in the Chilliwack River Valley, where seven RVs were removed from the forest near the Chilliwack River in January during a cleanup of abandoned encampments. Patti MacAhonic, director of Electoral Area E, said crews seem to be getting the upper hand, although she has accepted the problem will never be solved. The best they can do, she said, is manage it. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/it-can-cost-thousands-to-get-rid-of-an-old-rv-in-bc-so-people-are-dumping-them)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **October home sales fell ten per cent across Metro Vancouver, giving buyers more choice and sellers less leverage.**

**What You Need to Know:** October home sales fell ten per cent across Metro Vancouver, giving buyers more choice and sellers less leverage. Greater Vancouver Realtors counted 2,024 sales, and the composite benchmark is $1,068,600, down 5.2 per cent from a year ago. A Burnaby school-district database has been posted on a dark-web site, and a shuttle-bus crash near Mackenzie injured about 20 people.

### Top Stories
**Metro Vancouver home sales fall 10 per cent as Fraser Valley remains in buyer’s market: Real Estate Magazine Canada**
Greater Vancouver Realtors says 2,024 homes sold in October, 10.2 per cent fewer than a year earlier and 22.5 per cent below the 10-year average for the month. Andrew Lis, the board’s chief economist, said a Bank of Canada rate hike, the snap provincial election, and uncertainty about mortgage rates led buyers and sellers to step back. The composite benchmark fell to $1,068,600, down 5.2 per cent from October 2025 and 0.7 per cent from September. Detached homes are at $1,775,200, apartments at $673,400, and townhouses at $1,006,500. New listings fell 11.6 per cent to 4,805, while 15,688 active listings are still 24 per cent above the 10-year norm, and the sales-to-active ratio is 13.4 per cent. In Fraser Valley Real Estate Board territory, which includes Surrey, both Langleys, White Rock, and North Delta, sales rose 14 per cent from September to 1,051 but remained about 6 per cent under last October, and the benchmark is $860,000, down 6.4 per cent on the year. Board CEO Rock Lefebvre said much of the pandemic-era price growth has been erased, which he called the best affordability in five years, while warning that higher borrowing costs complicate that opening. Lis said markets were pricing a slight chance of another quarter-point hike at the Bank of Canada’s December update. Source: [realestatemagazine.ca](https://realestatemagazine.ca/metro-vancouver-home-sales-fall-10-per-cent-as-fraser-valley-remains-in-buyers-market/) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/metro-vancouver-fraser-valley-lower-mainland-home-sales-statistics-october-2026)

Police are asking anyone with dash-camera video, or who saw the bus in the minutes before the crash, to contact B.C. Highway Patrol in Prince George. He writes that the NDP vote is down more than 273,700, about 29 per cent, while the Greens have gained more than 23,500 votes and are leading in two seats. Turnout stands at 48.14 per cent, compared with 58.45 per cent in 2024, and mail-in and other absentee ballots are still to be counted. Harcourt says those figures leave little room for triumphalism, and that the Conservative government and the Opposition NDP now have to deliver practical improvements voters have been demanding. ### The Closer Look
**The Aristocratic sign glows again in neon exhibit at the Post: Vancouver Sun**
The giant neon sign for the Aristocratic restaurant is lit again at The Post, the office building in Vancouver’s former downtown post office. Last week the Museum of Vancouver lent it, with other pieces from its neon collection, to an installation called Lit! Neons of Vancouver. The signs are lined along a wall across from Deville Coffee at the 366 Dunsmuir Street entrance, facing the street. People can walk up to them while the building is open in the day, and they remain visible from the sidewalk at night.

The Aristocratic sign stood at Broadway and Granville from 1960 to 1997. It mixed red and blue neon, used four type styles, and carried a plastic panel of Risty, the restaurant’s mascot, a man in a top hat and monocle. The Vancouver Sun notes that in 1953 Neon Products counted 19,000 neon signs in the city, one for every 18 residents. The lot was later sold, the restaurant was demolished, and a Chapters bookstore was built there with a much smaller replica inside. The museum saved the original, three metres high, 3.3 metres long, and 0.3 metres deep, too big to fit through its doors. Aside from a brief spell hung outside the museum, it stayed in storage.

The restaurant was once part of a chain of 12 that started in 1928. The Broadway and Granville branch opened in 1938 and was the last one standing. A 1951 photograph shows a different Aristocratic sign at that corner; the sign now at The Post is the 1960 version. Beside it are a big “R” from the former Ridge Theatre at Arbutus Street and West 16th Avenue, a red-and-green Palm Ice Cream sign, the red neon of the American Hotel on Main Street, and a white neon sign for The Cookie Jar, a 1950s chain. The Ridge “R” went up in 1950 and came down when the theatre closed in 2013. It is lit by red neon and clear flashbulbs. The painted metal looks weathered after decades outside; the museum is keeping that patina. The other Ridge letters are still in Building 14, the warehouse where the museum keeps oversized objects, which is also where the Aristocratic sign had been stored. A 2001 replica of the Welding Shop and Engineering sign, which stood at 1600 Main Street from 1930 to 1974, is the only animated piece on display: a welder in a mask, a red torch, a green rod, and blue sparks that flash on and off.

Neon expert John Atkin told the Sun the signs sit at eye level, with overlapping colour the way they once worked on the street, and that the wall now has a purpose for people sitting with coffee. Karen Zajac, walking past, called the Aristocratic sign’s return fantastic and said one of her first dates was at the restaurant. The display has been in the works since 2019. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/the-aristocratic-sign-glows-again-in-neon-exhibit-at-the-post)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **116 Vancouver properties go to tax auction Wednesday, one reserved at $72,051.**

**What You Need to Know:** One hundred sixteen Vancouver properties go to a city tax auction on Wednesday, and one East Vancouver house assessed at more than $1.7 million carries a reserve of $72,051. Surrey police say the city recorded no extortion-related shooting from August through October, the longest stretch without one since the violence ramped up in summer 2025. On the central coast, a second person has been found dead after a suspected grizzly attack near Bella Coola.

### Top Stories
**This $1.7M Vancouver home has an auction reserve of $72K. Yes, there’s a catch: Global BC**
Global News reports that the City of Vancouver auctions 116 properties at city hall on Wednesday, starting at 10 a.m., in this year’s tax sale of homes whose owners have not paid taxes for three years. The reserve, or upset price, is the amount owed to the city. A Windsor Street house in East Vancouver, assessed by BC Assessment at more than $1.7 million, has a reserve of $72,051. Two side-by-side houses on Point Grey Road, valued around $5 million and $6 million, have upset prices of about $289,000 and $355,000. After auction day the current owners have a year to redeem by paying their taxes, which refunds the bidder plus interest. The city said there were only three instances in the last 10 years where a property changed hands from a tax sale, and that taxes on almost all properties have historically been paid within that year. The highest bidders must pay the upset price by noon Thursday. Retired notary Ron Usher said the law is structured to give the owner the maximum chance to sort the problem out, and that he suspects some sales are “whoops” rather than deliberate, citing inheritances. Realtor Sean Holden called bidding “an exercise in futility” and said he would not waste his time, citing how rarely sales are completed and the risk of not knowing a home’s condition. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12136233/this-1-7m-vancouver-home-has-an-auction-reserve-of-72k-yes-theres-a-catch/)

**Despite lull in Surrey extortion shootings, police not slowing down: Vancouver Sun**
Surrey recorded no extortion-related shooting from August through October, the longest stretch without one since the issue ramped up in summer 2025, the Vancouver Sun reports. Ian MacDonald, media liaison officer with the Surrey police, said police are pleased but will not stand down, and that the drop in shootings is not a sign the work is done. Extortion-related violence peaked in January, when police recorded 44 extortion threats and 10 of those cases involved shootings. Since the beginning of the year, Surrey police have had 147 extortion threats reported, 21 of them involving shootings. In 2025, 49 of 133 extortion cases reported to police involved shootings. MacDonald said that as of Sept. 14 the Canada Border Services Agency had issued 188 removal orders and deported 111 individuals related to extortion cases. He said some victims are still targeted after suspects are arrested or removed, so investigations that look closed often are not. He also said the crime is not limited to Punjabi-Canadian business owners: employees, neighbours, suppliers and security guards are affected too. A $250,000 City of Surrey reward fund for information leading to arrests and conviction remains active. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/surrey-extortion-shootings-update)

**Two dead in suspected bear attack near Bella Coola: Surrey Now-Leader**
The BC Conservation Officer Service said the second victim of a suspected grizzly attack near Bella Coola was found dead Tuesday afternoon during a search by conservation officers and the RCMP. Family members have identified the two people as Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, CBC reports. The pair were reported missing by family on Nov. 1. One person was found dead Monday afternoon, Nov. 2, in the Snooka West Trail area after a search involving the RCMP and Bella Coola Valley Search and Rescue; officers were called in after evidence suggested an animal may have been involved. The service said it is not clear whether more than one bear was involved, and that officers are still working to locate and capture any bears involved. Any bear captured will be assessed; if it is determined to be responsible, it will be dispatched under provincial human-wildlife conflict guidelines. People are urged to stay away from the Snooka West Trail area. On Nov. 20, 2025, an adult and three children were attacked by a grizzly at the Old Trail, close to 4 Mile. Elected Chief of the Nuxalk Nation Samuel Schooner said the nation knows the trauma this will inflict on the families, last year’s victim and the community, and asked residents to stay away from the trail, stay close to young children and keep spaces free of attractants. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/03/1-dead-1-missing-after-suspected-bear-attack-near-bella-coola/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bella-coola-grizzly-attack-9.7407640?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Park Board's public meetings moved to Vancouver City Hall on a pilot project basis: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Scheduled public meetings of Vancouver’s elected Park Board commissioners have moved, on a pilot, from the board’s headquarters at 2099 Beach Ave. to Vancouver City Council chambers at City Hall, Daily Hive reports. The change covers regular and committee meetings and is meant to make it easier for the public to attend and speak, and to encourage closer cooperation among the mayor, councillors and commissioners, a priority Mayor Pete Fry and the Green Party of Vancouver have identified. The first Park Board meeting at City Hall is Monday, Nov. 30, 2026, the first working meeting of this term. City Hall is near SkyTrain’s Broadway-City Hall station, served by the Canada Line and, starting in late 2027, the Millennium Line extension. The seven commissioners were sworn in Monday, Nov. 2, at VanDusen Botanical Garden. Green commissioner Tom Digby, the only incumbent, was elected the term’s first chair, and COPE’s Sacia Burton the first vice-chair. The other commissioners are COPE’s Jamie Han, Tamiko Suzuki and T’uy’t’tanat Cease Wyss, and the Green Party’s Spencer Van Vloten and Breanne Smart. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-park-board-meetings-relocated-city-hall)

**Major Sunshine Coast forestry operation bought for $80M by Tla'amin Nation: CBC British Columbia**
The Tla’amin Nation’s forestry arm has acquired a 100 per cent ownership interest in the Stillwater Forest Operation near Powell River for about $80 million after adjustments, CBC reports. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/sunshine-coast-forestry-operation-stillwater-tla-amin-9.7408247?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver Aquatic Centre demolition to proceed after interim injunction expires: CBC British Columbia**
Demolition of the Vancouver Aquatic Centre will proceed later this month, after an interim injunction expired on Tuesday, as part of a controversial renovation that includes a 25-metre pool, CBC reports. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-aquatic-centre-demolition-injunction-expires-9.7408069?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**'Preserving the best of West Vancouver': Read Mayor Kirk LaPointe's full inaugural speech: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Kirk LaPointe used his first speech as mayor of West Vancouver, after he and the new council were sworn in on the evening of Monday, November 2, to promise residents a greater voice in decisions, careful spending, and room for more people to build lives in the community. He defeated incumbent Mark Sager in last month’s civic election.

His career runs through newsrooms: managing editor of the Vancouver Sun, executive editor of the National Post, CBC ombudsman for English services, publisher and executive editor of Business in Vancouver, and an executive at Glacier Media, now Lodestar Media, until 2023. He has taught journalism at the University of British Columbia. He lives in Caulfeild. In 2014 he ran unsuccessfully for Vancouver mayor for the Non-Partisan Association, against Gregor Robertson.

On the campaign he promised to bring the projected 2027 municipal tax increase down from nearly seven per cent to three per cent, and after 2027 to cap annual municipal spending growth at half the inflation rate. He promised to eliminate municipal pay parking, to revitalize the commercial villages of Ambleside, Dundarave, Horseshoe Bay and Caulfeild, and to seek provincial permission for a tax on vacant storefronts. His housing pitch was smaller-scale multi-unit housing for seniors, young families and first responders, while preserving neighbourhood character. An urgent and primary care centre was his first priority for a public-private partnership. He also proposed arts, skating and seniors’ facilities, restoring advisory committees, twice-monthly public question-and-answer sessions, and fewer closed-door council meetings. At Metro Vancouver he said he would push for an independent review of the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant, changes to its funding formula and repayment period, and no additional regional compensation.

He told the inauguration that council cannot promise everyone the answer they want, but can promise respect, openness and an honest account of decisions. Preserving the best of West Vancouver and preparing for its future, he said, are one promise, like old trees rooted deep enough to withstand storms that still put out new growth each spring. He thanked Mark Sager and councillors Sharon Thompson, Christine Cassidy and Nora Gambioli. He serves with returning councillors Linda Watt, Peter Lambur and Scott Snider, and new councillors Lee Lau, Jaime Webbe and Tim Webb. Lau’s background is medicine and clinical leadership, Webbe’s is international diplomacy, executive leadership and financial management, and Webb’s is local business and commercial property. He noted that long before any of them arrived, the Squamish people knew these shores, rivers and mountains. Earlier Monday, he said, council met to share what the campaigns had taught them about what West Vancouver wants, so they can develop the plans to deliver it. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/kirk-lapointe-west-vancouver-mayor-inaugural-speech-november-2026)

### Also Today
**Social media site X can't be fined for refusing to delete intimate image, B.C. civil tribunal rules: Vancouver Sun**
A B.C. civil tribunal ruled X cannot be fined for refusing to delete an intimate image; the company geoblocked the image in Canada and said an order to delete it would infringe on free-speech laws in the United States. Three new Vancouver bookstores are being founded by former employees of McLeod’s Books. Source: [vancouverisawesome.com](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/local-news/three-new-bookstores-opening-in-vancouver-12976020)

**Surrey golf course strike enters month 2, boycott called after alleged vehicle strike: CityNews**
Workers at a Surrey golf course are entering a second month on strike, and the BC Federation of Labour is calling a boycott after a union representative said she was struck by a vehicle on the picket line. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/video/2026/11/03/workers-on-strike-calling-out-alleged-violence-at-surrey-golf-course/)

A vehicle incident on Highway 17 in Delta, before 80th Street and the Tilbury Connector, has the right lane blocked; DriveBC’s last update was 6:16 a.m., with a next update set for 7:15 a.m. On Highway 99 in Delta at the Delta Works Yard, traffic is reduced to one lane and DriveBC says to expect major delays from congestion, last updated at 5:50 a.m. Highway 1 is closed from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford, all day every day until Dec. 31, with a detour and eastbound traffic shifted south of the median. The Royal Avenue onramp in New Westminster closes from 9 p.m. Thursday, Nov. 5, until 5 a.m. Saturday, Nov. 7, overnight Thursday and Friday, with a detour via Royal Avenue to McBride Boulevard and then the Columbia Street onramp. Night work on Highway 99 from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17 runs 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., Monday to Saturday, until Nov. 8, with one lane each way kept open. Environment Canada has no watches or warnings for Vancouver. It is clear and 4.2 degrees this morning, with fog patches dissipating, then mainly sunny and a high of 11, cloud increasing early this afternoon, and a UV index of 2. Rain begins this evening, with a low of 7 and southeast wind at 20 km/h becoming southwest overnight. ### Sports
**Gauthier has second straight hat trick, Ducks hold off Canucks' late rally: NHL.com**
Cutter Gauthier scored his second straight hat trick and the Anaheim Ducks held off the Vancouver Canucks 5-4 at Rogers Arena on Tuesday, NHL.com reports. Gauthier is the first player in Ducks history with back-to-back hat tricks and has eight goals in the past three games after nine without a goal. Beckett Sennecke had a career-high four assists, all primary, including the passes on all three Gauthier goals. Mikael Granlund had a goal and two assists. The Ducks’ power play was 3-for-3. Jake DeBrusk scored twice in the third for Vancouver. Kevin Lankinen made 17 saves; Laurent Brossoit made 19. The Canucks are 3-13-1, and their only win in 14 games came in overtime on Oct. 27 against these Ducks.
