# Vancouver Daily News
> **Eight court challenges now target an oil pipeline bound for Tsawwassen.**

**What You Need to Know:** Eight separate Federal Court challenges now target Ottawa’s national-interest designation for the Pacific Link oil pipeline, planned to end at a new marine terminal in Tsawwassen. Vancouver and Surrey swore in new councils Monday, and homicide charges have been laid in the death of an 11-year-old Burnaby boy who had been missing for more than a year.

### Top Stories
**Pete Fry sworn in as Vancouver's 42nd mayor promising 'collaboration over division': CBC British Columbia**
Pete Fry was sworn in Monday as Vancouver’s 42nd mayor, the city’s first Green mayor, after defeating incumbent Ken Sim of ABC Vancouver in the October 17 election. Speaking at the city-owned Orpheum Theatre, Fry said, “I may be mayor, but I’m also a neighbour, and being a good neighbour means listening carefully.” He said disagreement does not have to become division, and closed with “Let’s get to work.” No party has a majority. All four Green candidates were elected — Annette Reilly, Camil Dumont, Bridget Burns and Stephanie Smith — along with four COPE candidates: Sean Orr, returned for a second term, and new councillors Chloe Leslie, Devyani Singh and Solomon Yi-Kieran. OneCity’s Lucy Maloney and ABC’s Mike Klassen are each their party’s only member; both said they looked forward to working with the new council. After the ceremony Fry held a press conference with all 10 councillors, from COPE, OneCity, ABC Vancouver and the Green Party. Park board commissioners and school board trustees were sworn in the same day. The crowd included former mayors Kennedy Stewart and Larry Campbell, and Fry’s mother, Liberal MP Hedy Fry. Fred Lee was master of ceremonies. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/pete-fry-mayor-inauguration-9.7406488?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/new-vancouver-mayor-council-sworn-in) Source: [vancouverisawesome.com](https://www.vancouverisawesome.com/economy-law-politics/inauguration-day-pete-fry-newly-elected-vancouver-city-councillors-take-oath-of-office-12971667)

**Doug McCallum sworn in as Mayor of Surrey, Mandeep Nagra as Deputy Mayor: Indo-Canadian Voice**
Doug McCallum was sworn in Monday evening as mayor of Surrey, with Mandeep Nagra as deputy mayor. McCallum, also mayor from 1996 to 2005 and from 2018 to 2022, begins a fifth term. He thanked the city for its trust and said premier-designate Lorne Doerkson had committed to a new women’s and children’s hospital in Surrey and to SkyTrain down King George Boulevard to Newton. McCallum repeatedly said there would be no increase in property taxes, and said Surrey is going to be an economic powerhouse in B.C. and in Canada. Surrey Now-Leader reported the new council as five women and four men, sworn in with ceremony and no business on the agenda. Source: [voiceonline.com](https://voiceonline.com/doug-mccallum-sworn-in-as-mayor-of-surrey-mandeep-nagra-as-deputy-mayor/) Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/02/all-ceremony-no-business-5-women-4-men-sworn-in-as-new-surrey-city-council/)

**Family members charged in homicide of missing 11-year-old Burnaby boy: CBC British Columbia**
Police say 11-year-old Kai Pavlovic was killed before he was reported missing on September 26, 2025. More than a year after Burnaby RCMP received a request that day to check on his wellbeing, investigators have recovered his body and charged family members in his death. CityNews reported that the alleged offences took place before the boy was reported missing. The people charged are accused; the charges are not findings of guilt. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/kai-pavlovic-homicide-charges-burnaby-bc-9.7405999?cmp=rss) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12130166/charged-missing-11-year-old-bc-boy-remains-found/) Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/video/2026/11/02/missing-burnaby-boy-found-dead-family-members-charged/)

**B.C. seizes Vancouver Island couple's bank accounts, alleges insider trading: Vancouver Sun**
B.C.’s director of civil forfeiture has seized seven bank and investment accounts belonging to David and Leslie Finn of Nanoose Bay, alleging insider trading ahead of the sale of Sabina Gold and Silver Corp. A lawsuit in B.C. Supreme Court says the couple bought almost 500,000 Sabina shares for about $685,000 between October 2022 and February 10, 2023, the day B2Gold Corp. announced it was buying Sabina. In October 2022 they owned only a nominal number of shares, the lawsuit says. It alleges the purchases are “indicative of prohibited insider trading” and that the accounts are proceeds and instruments of unlawful activity under the Civil Forfeiture Act, citing the Criminal Code and the B.C. Securities Act. The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization flagged more than 100 investors who bought $10,000 or more of Sabina shares in the 40 days before the announcement. The lawsuit says a TD account in Leslie Finn’s name, over which David Finn had power of attorney, was used to buy 150,000 shares worth $232,000 the day the sale was announced. None of the allegations has been proven in court. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-seizes-vancouver-island-bank-accounts-alleges-insider-trading)

### City & Province
**Difficult and unpopular decisions ahead, B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson says: Business in Vancouver**
Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said Monday the B.C. Conservative caucus of 63 newly elected legislators is united to lead the province, and warned of difficult and unpopular decisions ahead. He said he will swear in the new MLAs and appoint a cabinet at the first opportunity. Columnist Vaughn Palmer wrote that the timetable leaves room to recall the legislature this fall. Separately, CBC reported that Doerkson’s promise to roll back provincial housing targets has some municipal leaders feeling hopeful after previous goals proved challenging for some. That rollback remains a promise, not a decision in force. Source: [biv.com](https://www.biv.com/news/difficult-and-unpopular-decisions-ahead-bc-premier-designate-lorne-doerkson-says-12969530) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/vaughn-palmer-bc-conservatives-signal-intent-fast-track-changes) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/mayors-respond-housing-targets-repeal-9.7406239?cmp=rss)

**Former junior league hockey executive accused of child sexual exploitation: Global BC**
Alberta RCMP say Tyler King, 39, was arrested Friday at a Canada-U.S. border crossing in Ontario and charged with three counts of luring a person under 18, sexual exploitation of a young person, and making child pornography. Police say three players, all under 18 at the time and from Saskatchewan and Alberta, were victimized. An Okotoks Oilers employee told police in June 2024 that a former staff member was soliciting and compensating players for intimate videos and pictures. King later worked for the Nanaimo Clippers Junior A team; police said it is unlikely that club knew of the allegations when he was hired, and that there may be further victims in B.C., Saskatchewan, Ontario, Fort McMurray and Brooks. He is charged, not convicted. The investigation remains active, and the RCMP is asking any victims to speak with police. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12130449/tyler-king-sex-crimes-youth/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/calgary/okotoks-oilers-tyler-king-sexual-assualt-arrest-9.7406208?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**B.C. ostrich farm files lawsuit against CFIA, government and RCMP: Surrey Now-Leader**
Universal Ostrich Farm and Landco Ventures filed a multi-million-dollar civil claim on October 30 against the Canadian Food Inspection Agency, the Attorney General of Canada and the RCMP. The claim comes almost a year after the flock at their Edgewood farm, in B.C.’s Interior, was killed. Farm representatives Karen Espersen and Katiey Pasitney, a mother and daughter, say 351 ostriches were killed on November 6 and 7, 2025. They describe a 35-year family legacy and say the suit seeks justice, accountability and policy change.

They say the claim arises from what they call aggressive and intrusive regulatory action that culminated in a 52-day occupation of the property, the forced slaughter of the flock, and the destruction of a commercial enterprise. They date an alleged unlawful search and occupation by the CFIA and the RCMP to on or about September 3, 2025. The pleadings also allege inadequate statutory compensation, animal cruelty, missing birds, unlawful seizure of ostrich eggs, property damage and trespassing. A CBC report on the same filing says the owners accuse the federal government of animal cruelty, under-compensation and preventing the launch of a lucrative commercial enterprise, and that the claim concerns 37 birds they say were missing after the 2025 cull.

The relief they seek includes an order that the defendants remove encroachments and remediate the property; a complete accounting and the return of, or compensation for, removed documents, materials, birds and eggs; and general, special, punitive and exemplary damages for trespass, nuisance, intrusion upon seclusion, harassment, negligence and Charter breaches, plus damages for permanent devaluation of the land. Espersen and Pasitney said they cannot bring the birds back, and that the lawsuit is about protecting rights and transparency as well as compensation.

American billionaire John Catsimatidis, who supported the farm’s effort last year to have the ostriches tested before they were killed, said he was disappointed the CFIA did not allow Secretary Kennedy, Dr. Oz or the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to test the birds as requested. He suggested that decision contributed to tensions between the two countries, and said he hopes the countries can work more closely again. None of the accusations has been proven in court. Source: [surreynowleader.com](https://surreynowleader.com/2026/11/02/b-c-ostrich-farm-files-lawsuit-against-cfia-government-and-rcmp/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/ostrich-farm-lawsuit-9.7406462?cmp=rss)

### Also Today
**Suhana Gill, 20-year-old Punjab-origin woman, becomes youngest-ever councillor in Canada's Surrey: The Tribune**
The Tribune reports that Suhana Gill, 20, is the youngest person ever sworn in as a Surrey city councillor. Source: [tribuneindia.com](https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/suhana-gill-20-year-old-punjab-origin-woman-becomes-youngest-ever-councillor-in-canadas-surrey/)

**Surrey Police say vehicle and driver identified in suspicious incident: Indo-Canadian Voice**
Surrey Police Service said Monday the vehicle it asked the public to help identify on November 1 has been located and the driver identified, after a man in a white Toyota Corolla spoke to two teenage girls in the 10100-block of 123A Street at about 3:30 p.m. on October 27; the investigation is ongoing. Source: [voiceonline.com](https://voiceonline.com/surrey-police-say-vehicle-and-driver-identified-in-suspicious-incident/)

**Adam Kai-Ji Lo, accused in Vancouver’s Lapu Lapu Day attack, pleads not guilty: CFJC Today Kamloops**
Adam Kai-Ji Lo, accused in the Lapu Lapu Day attack in Vancouver, has pleaded not guilty. Source: [cfjctoday.com](https://cfjctoday.com/2026/11/02/adam-kai-ji-lo-accused-in-vancouvers-lapu-lapu-day-attack-pleads-not-guilty/)

**Bryan Yu: B.C. small business confidence slumps in October: Business in Vancouver**
Business in Vancouver columnist Bryan Yu reports that nearly 20 percent of B.C. businesses plan to cut full-time staff as small-business confidence slumped in October. Source: [biv.com](https://www.biv.com/small-business/bryan-yu-bc-small-business-confidence-slumps-in-october-12970531)

**VIDEO: Vehicle flips, ends up in water-filled ditch in Surrey, 2 hospitalized: Peace Arch News**
Peace Arch News reports that a vehicle flipped into a water-filled ditch in Surrey and two people were taken to hospital. Source: [peacearchnews.com](https://peacearchnews.com/2026/11/02/video-vehicle-flips-ends-up-in-water-filled-ditch-in-surrey-2-hospitalized/)

**Where is Jennifer? After almost 2 years, rural B.C. mom of three still missing: Global BC**
Jennifer Provencal, 51, was last seen on February 5, 2025, by her husband, Tom Boulding, who said they had argued at their rural B.C. home. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12130347/mother-missing-rural-bc-home-almost-2-years-jennifer-provencal/)

### Getting Around
Highway 1 is closed from 256th Street in Langley to Lefeuvre Road in Abbotsford through December 31, 2026, all day, every day, with a detour and eastbound traffic shifted south of the median. On Highway 7 in Maple Ridge, DriveBC lists the right lane closed today from 203 Street to Dewdney Trunk Road between 9 a.m. and 3 p.m. Night work on Highway 99 in Delta, from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17, runs until November 8 from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., Monday to Saturday, with one lane open each way. The Royal Avenue on-ramp in New Westminster is set for overnight closure from 9 p.m. Thursday, November 5, to 5 a.m. Saturday, November 7, with a detour via Royal Avenue to McBride Boulevard and the Columbia Street on-ramp. No weather watches or warnings are in effect. Vancouver is mostly cloudy and 8.2 degrees this morning; Tuesday is cloudy with a 30 percent chance of showers this morning and a high of 11, clearing tonight to a low of 5. Wednesday is mainly sunny, then cloudier, with a high of 12, and Wednesday night turns rainy and windy with a low of 10. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Game Notes: Canucks vs. Ducks: NHL.com**
The Anaheim Ducks visit the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Arena tonight, with puck drop at 6 p.m. Pacific, on Sportsnet in Vancouver. Anaheim is 6-7-1 with 13 points; Vancouver is 3-12-1 with 7 points. This is the second of four meetings; on October 27 in Anaheim the Canucks won 6-5 in overtime, with Filip Hronek scoring the winner. Vancouver’s last game, October 31 against Toronto, ended 2-4. The Canucks recalled Jacob Quillan from Abbotsford on October 30, with Filip Chytil on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Anaheim recalled Nico Myatovic, from Prince George, and placed A.J. Greer on injured reserve. Players including Brock Boeser have praised the club’s new blue-on-blue Hometown Remix jersey. The Canucks’ next listed game after tonight is November 5 against the Winnipeg Jets. Source: [nhl.com](https://www.nhl.com/canucks/news/game-notes-canucks-vs-ducks-11-0326) Source: [insidetherink.com](https://insidetherink.com/nhl-game-preview-anaheim-ducks-at-vancouver-canucks-with-line-combinations-11-03-2026/) Source: [canucksarmy.com](https://canucksarmy.com/news/big-fan-ones-brock-boeser-vancouver-canucks-players-rave-hometown-remix-jerseys-helmets)

### What's On
**Columnist shares complex story of growing up as the child of Holocaust survivors: North Shore News**
Vancouver-based Globe and Mail columnist Marsha Lederman speaks in West Vancouver on November 4 about her memoir, Kiss the Red Stairs: The Holocaust, Once Removed. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/columnist-shares-complex-story-of-growing-up-as-the-child-of-holocaust-survivors-12969666)

**Out and About: Art auction pieces on display at Richmond Art Gallery: Richmond News**
Auction artwork is on display at the Richmond Art Gallery until Saturday, November 21, and bids are open now. Source: [richmond-news.com](https://www.richmond-news.com/opinion/art-auction-pieces-on-display-at-richmond-bc-art-gallery-12971337)

### Both Sides: Pacific Link pipeline
Ottawa’s national-interest designation for the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline is now the subject of eight separate Federal Court challenges from First Nations in B.C. The line, the first project designated under the Building Canada Act, would move an additional one million barrels a day from the Edmonton area to a new marine export terminal in Tsawwassen, largely along the Trans Mountain corridor. Global News puts the estimated cost between $35.2 billion and $42.7 billion. The final route still depends on design, review, consultation and approvals. Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson has pledged to work with Alberta and Ottawa to advance it, with major ongoing economic benefits for B.C. in return.

The federal case, as set out when Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith announced the designation last month, is that the line would reach more Asian customers, reduce dependence on the United States, and give Alberta, B.C. and Ottawa a long-term revenue source. Indigenous communities are to be offered at least a 10 percent ownership interest, backed by federal and Alberta loan guarantees. The Major Projects Office said it had consulted more than 130 Indigenous communities over three months; further consultation would set conditions, which Ottawa aims to finalize by September 2027 so construction can begin. National-interest status gives advance federal approval subject to those conditions, folding permits into one document.

The case against, from the nations filing, is that the designation was made without the consultation the law requires and without an impact assessment. St’át’imc Chiefs Council chair Justin Kane said the threat of a spill to Fraser River salmon, fishing rights and “our way of being” is heinous, and that the St’át’imc Nation as a whole was not consulted. The council, representing 11 communities, says the proposal means more than 500 river crossings, including two new Fraser crossings, and would increase tanker traffic in the Salish Sea. Tsartlip spokesman Adam Olsen called the process reckless and rushed, completed in less than three months for a project not expected to be finished until 2032, in fishing areas the nation is responsible for. Elder Art Adolph said governments and industry would push First Nations further into third-world conditions through harm to wild salmon. Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, president of the Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs, told corporations to beware when investing in B.C., because “we are not standing down.” Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12130609/bc-first-nations-file-challenges-pacific-link-pipeline-decision/) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/bc-first-nations-lawsuit-pacific-link-oil-pipeline-national-interest) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-first-nations-file-court-challenge-against-proposed-pacific-link-pipeline)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **One person is dead after a Friday house fire on Young Road in Chilliwack.**

**What You Need to Know:** One person is dead after a Friday house fire on Young Road in Chilliwack, and the Chilliwack Fire Department says the origin and cause are still under investigation. In Nelson, three bystanders pulled a driver from a pickup that left a mall lot and went into Kootenay Lake. In Vancouver, testing has not turned up any further rabid skunks, and the animal that was tested carried the bat variant.

### Top Stories
**Blaze kills one in Chilliwack home fire: CityNews**
A blaze broke out at a home on Young Road in Chilliwack on Friday afternoon and left one person dead, the Chilliwack Fire Department confirms. Crews were called to the 9800 block of the street around 2:15 p.m. When they arrived, they learned that one person might still be inside the home. In a news release Friday night, the department said firefighters worked to extinguish the fire and located an individual inside the home. The department said that individual was pronounced deceased at the scene. Fire crews said the house had extensive fire, smoke and water damage, which kept the other residents from returning Friday night. The department said the origin and cause of the fire remain under investigation. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/11/01/chilliwack-fire-fatal/)

**Samaritans rescue truck from Kootenay Lake: CityNews**
Three good Samaritans jumped into Kootenay Lake in Nelson on Saturday to go after a truck that drove over the embankment and into the water. Nelson Police Department said it received 911 calls around 1:18 p.m. saying a truck had left the parking lot of Chahko Mika Mall and landed in the lake. CBC reported the vehicle was a pickup and that the driver was a woman. The three who dove in were able to rescue her from the sinking truck. Nelson’s police, fire department and BC Emergency Health Services attended and found the driver had already been pulled from the water. She was checked by paramedics and released without being taken to hospital. Drugs or alcohol have been ruled out as a possible cause. The incident remains under investigation. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/11/01/nelson-kootenay-lake-truck/) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/witnesses-rescue-driver-from-submerged-vehicle-in-kootenay-lake-9.7405004?cmp=rss)

**After testing, no further rabid skunks found in Vancouver: The Tyee**
Testing has not found any further rabid skunks in Vancouver. A small number of people received post-exposure care. The skunk that was tested had tested positive for the bat variant of rabies. Source: [thetyee.ca](https://thetyee.ca/News/2026/11/02/No-Further-Rabid-Skunks-Vancouver/)

### City & Province
**Doerkson says preference is for public servants to return to the office: CBC British Columbia**
British Columbia’s incoming premier, Lorne Doerkson, says his preference is to see teleworking public servants return to the office environment. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-public-service-remote-hybrid-return-to-office-9.7404947?cmp=rss)

**Phones showed the wrong time after the West stayed on daylight time: Global BC**
After British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, northwestern Ontario and the Northwest Territories stayed on daylight time year-round rather than falling back an hour, some Canadians reported Sunday that their cellphones displayed the incorrect time. Saskatchewan already does not adjust its clocks. A statement from Telus says the issue is related to how some phones update their time-zone information, rather than the service provider. Telus says customers can check that “set time zone automatically” is selected, then restart the phone to help apply any available time-zone updates. A Rogers spokesperson said the company experienced no issues with its network and referred questions to an industry group that posted instructions for updating phones and tablets. Air Canada said Sunday its operations were normal, noting that all flights use the internationally recognized time standard and that time changes are managed using established industry data sources. Google responded to an inquiry by linking to a blog post with instructions for keeping devices and services on schedule, and said its teams are working to ensure the updates reach all Canadian users as quickly as possible. The post said people rely on devices for morning alarms and critical calendar invites. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12129795/western-canada-time-change/)

**B.C. beer league hockey player acquitted of assault: CBC British Columbia**
A B.C. man has been acquitted of aggravated assault and uttering threats over an incident during a beer-league hockey game that left another player with serious head injuries. The case concerned a rival struck in the face with a stick. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/beer-league-assault-acquitted-9.7404335?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**It's a prime time for classical music in Vancouver: Vancouver Sun**
November is prime time for classical music in Vancouver, and the Vancouver Sun’s concert docket for the month is full of dated shows at named rooms. The month opens with the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra on November 6 and 7 at 7:30 p.m. at the Orpheum. Guest conductor Antony Hermus, until recently chief conductor of the Belgian National Orchestra, offers an all-Russian program: rarely heard Scriabin to start, and Prokofiev’s fairy-tale ballet music for Cinderella to end. The anchoring work is Shostakovich’s First Violin Concerto, with American violinist Kevin Zhu. The Sun notes that the orchestra prides itself on its way with Russian repertoire. That same weekend, mezzo-soprano Ema Nikolovska and guitarist Sean Shibe return with their Orlando Project on November 8 at 3 p.m. at the Telus Studio Theatre in the Chan Centre for the Performing Arts. The program runs from Dowland to Bob Dylan, framed as a musical reflection of Ariosto’s Orlando Furioso and Virginia Woolf’s 1928 novel Orlando: A Biography. The following Sunday, the Vancouver Recital Society presents harpsichordist Jean Rondeau playing Couperin and Rameau at the Barnet Recital Hall on November 15 at 3 p.m. The Sun says the room, in the University of British Columbia’s School of Music, is small, and that Rondeau has a dedicated following, so tickets need to be secured quickly. Chor Leoni’s Remembrance Day concert, The Soul Flies Away, is the choir’s 35th annual event of that kind, at 2 p.m. and 5 p.m. on November 11 at St. Andrew’s-Wesley church. Two days later, two concerts occupy the same hour. Early Music Vancouver presents The Magic of Monteverdi by the French ensemble Les Arts Florissants, co-directed by William Christie and Paul Agnew, on November 17 at 7:30 p.m. at the Chan Centre. The program draws on Monteverdi’s books of madrigals for mixed voices, including the proto-opera Il Combattimento di Tancredi e Clorinda. At the same time, downtown at the Vancouver Playhouse, Friends of Chamber Music hosts the Terra String Quartet, winner of the 2025 Naumburg Chamber Music Competition and a prizewinner at the 2025 Bordeaux and Wigmore Hall International String Quartet Competitions. Terra plays late Beethoven, arrangements of madrigals by Maddalena Casulana, and Benjamin Britten’s Third String Quartet, drawn from his final opera, Death in Venice. At month’s end, Thomas Dunford’s Jupiter Ensemble returns for the Vancouver Recital Society on November 29 at 3 p.m. at the Chan Centre, with Italian, German and French baroque music unified by the legend of the Amazons. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/entertainment/vancouver-classical-music-concerts-november-2026)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Three-quarters of Metro Vancouver homes sold this year went for less than assessed value.**

**What You Need to Know:** Three-quarters of homes sold across Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley this year went for less than assessed value, Zealty.ca found. Unionized public sector workers rallied Saturday at Vancouver International Airport against federal plans to privatize operations. Vancouver police arrested a 38-year-old man within 10 minutes of a West End bank-robbery call on Friday.

### Top Stories
**Majority of Metro Vancouver homes selling at below assessed value: Vancouver Sun**
Zealty.ca, a B.C. real estate data platform, found that three-quarters of homes sold across Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley this year sold for below their assessed value. The Vancouver Sun described that housing data as another example of the region's struggling residential resale market. The supplied report does not break the share down by city, property type, or month, so the figure stands as a region-wide count for sales so far this year, covering both Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/business/real-estate/metro-vancouver-homes-selling-below-assessed-value)

**Unions rally against plan to privatize operation of Vancouver airport: CBC British Columbia**
Unionized public sector workers gathered at Vancouver International Airport, YVR, on Saturday to rally against federal plans to privatize the operation of the facility. CBC British Columbia reported the gathering as a protest aimed at those federal plans for how the airport is run. The supplied account names the workers as unionized public sector staff and places them at the airport itself, not at a legislature or a downtown square. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-airport-privatization-rally-9.7402960?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver bank robbery suspect quickly found and arrested, police say: CBC British Columbia**
Vancouver police say a 38-year-old man was arrested within 10 minutes of officers being called to a robbery in progress in the city's West End Friday afternoon. Police describe him as arrested in connection with that call, not as convicted. The supplied account gives the age, the neighbourhood, the Friday afternoon timing, and the 10-minute window between the call and the arrest, and it identifies the call as a robbery in progress. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-bank-robbery-arrest-9.7404358?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Aggravation? 'Absolutely': How B.C.'s time change affects businesses on both sides of the border: Vancouver Sun**
With B.C. staying on daylight time, the province will be an hour ahead of Western U.S. states, a shift the Vancouver Sun says requires some adjustment for businesses on both sides of the border. The Sun's headline frames that cross-border gap as aggravation. The piece is about the hour difference itself and the adjustment it forces on firms that work both sides of the line, not about a new vote. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/local-news/how-bc-time-change-affects-businesses-us-border)

**Vancouver remains committed to trolleybuses in the long term – off-wire capability could open up new possibilities: Magyarbusz**
Vancouver remains committed to trolleybuses in the long term, Magyarbusz reports, and off-wire capability could open up new possibilities for that fleet. What it does state is a long-term commitment to trolleybuses, with off-wire running described as a capability that could widen what those buses can do. Source: [magyarbusz.info](https://magyarbusz.info/en/2026/11/01/vancouver-remains-committed-to-trolleybuses-in-the-long-term-off-wire-capability-could-open-up-new-possibilities/)

### The Closer Look
**The 10 must-see concerts in Vancouver this November: Vancouver Sun**
November in Vancouver is packed with dated shows, and the Vancouver Sun's list treats the month as the last stretch before holiday songs take over the speakers. The paper notes that early fall is harvest and Halloween, that decorations go up almost as soon as the jack-o'-lantern candle goes out, and that Remembrance Day is the month's most solemn mark. Against that, it offers 10 shows, most of them with a night, a time, and a room.

The Jade Music Festival runs November 3 to 8 at various times and enters its fifth year larger than ever. Its stated goal is elevating Chinese-language music in Canada and around the world. The Sun points to Vancouver-based jazzy R&B artist Kristin Fung as one way in, among Canadian and international acts working cross-cultural traditions.

Crazy Diamonds, a Vancouver Pink Floyd tribute with two decades of live work, plays November 14 at 8 p.m. The Sun's case for a tribute is that seeing Pink Floyd itself is something no one will experience again, because the surviving members rarely perform live. Tyla plays November 15 at 8 p.m. at the Doug Mitchell Thunderbird Sports Centre at UBC. The Sun calls her the youngest South African artist in history to win a Grammy, and the "Queen of Popiano," a hybrid of pop and South African amapiano beats. It cites this year's album A*Pop and songs Chanel and That Girl, and says the live show is full of dance.

Art d'Ecco, the Vancouver Island singer presently appearing in the Crave comedy series I Kill The Bear, plays November 20 at 8 p.m. at the Rickshaw Theatre, 254 East Hastings. The new album is titled Scheele's Green, after a colour first mixed by artist Carl Wilhelm Scheele in 1775, and the Sun says the release finds him rocking hard with his backing band. On November 25 at 8 p.m., the Vogue Theatre at 918 Granville Street hosts an all-ages bill led by Gwar, with Midnight, Mac Sabbath, and Nailed Shut also on it. The Sun calls it a loud, sweaty night.

The Pointed Sticks play a farewell, billed Last Hurrah, on November 28 at 8 p.m. The Sun calls them a legendary Vancouver New Wave group that put out some of the best singles of that era, skirted global success, later reunited for new records and tours to Europe, Japan, and elsewhere, and is now bidding fans farewell one last time. The same date, November 28, from 6 p.m. to 2 a.m., DJ Tiësto headlines an all-ages EDM festival at Tradex, 1190 Cornell Street in Abbotsford, with Aaron Hibell, Benwal, Darude, Dash Berlin, Matty Ralph, and Modeā. On November 29 at 8 p.m., Edmonton-based tenor saxophonist Jacob Do leads a band at Frankie's Jazz Club, 755 Beatty Street, around his debut album First Chorus on MacEwan University's Bent River Records. The Sun says he was already an award-winning musician before he graduated, and names alto saxophonist Steve Kaldestad, pianist Tilden Webb, bassist Dan Howard, and drummer Joe Poole. One listing in the same piece, Bonobo, is dated March 16 at 8 p.m., not November, with a new album and a live show designed by stage artist Pierre Claude. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/entertainment/the-10-must-see-concerts-in-vancouver-this-november)

Monday is a mix of sun and cloud with a high of 11, Monday night is cloudy with a low of 6, and Tuesday is cloudy with a high of 13. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Matthews, Nylander lead Leafs to win over Canucks: Global BC**
The Vancouver Canucks lost 4-2 to the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday at home and are 3-12-1, with one win in their last 13 games, a stretch Pacific North Hockey recorded as 1-11-1. Toronto is 8-6-2 and finished a four-game road trip 2-2-0, snapping a two-game skid. William Nylander opened the scoring 83 seconds in, scooping a puck off Jamie Oleksiak's stick for a breakaway and lifting a backhand past Leevi Meriläinen. Brock Boeser tied it on the power play about nine minutes later, his fifth goal of the season, taking a stretch pass from Filip Hronek and beating Anthony Stolarz. Boeser told reporters he and Hronek had been looking for that pass for a few games, and he later said the league is too good to take a period off.

Auston Matthews scored his team-leading 11th at 3:47 of the second, beating Meriläinen short side after a pass with Darren Raddysh, for a 2-1 lead. He came into the night with 10 goals and now has 46 shots through 15 games. Editor In Leaf reported a point in every road game this season, seven goals and 15 points, and an eight-game road point streak, the longest by a Leaf since Doug Gilmour's 12-game stretch in 1993-94. Zack MacEwen, who played 62 games for Vancouver, scored the winner at 12:34 of the second. Daily Hive and Canadian Press described a point shot that came off Meriläinen's glove, hit Luke Schenn in the back, and rolled in. Teddy Blueger, 198 games as a Canuck, assisted on that goal and scored the empty-netter at 18:24 of the third after Stolarz tried to fire the puck up the ice. Nylander and Blueger each finished with a goal and an assist. Dakota Joshua, back for his first game of the season after a core injury and a veteran of 212 Canucks games, had five shots and seven hits. Chris Tanev, 537 games in Vancouver, played his first game since an upper-body injury on October 10 at Colorado. He told Sportsnet's Dan Murphy he was nervous coming back after three weeks off against a team that works hard and is desperate for a win.

Max Sasson scored his fourth of the season at 9:27 of the third, off the rebound of a Brendan Gallagher shot after Paul Cotter gained the zone, to make it 3-2. Sasson said the fourth line with Cotter and Gallagher is trying to be simple. Meriläinen made 24 saves in a fourth straight start and stopped first-overall pick Gavin McKenna on a first-period power play, a cross-ice pass from Jack Roslovic. Stolarz stopped 26 of 28 shots for his fifth win, with a 2.66 goals-against average and a .910 save percentage, and picked up his third assist of the season. Even-strength shot attempts were 22-12 Vancouver in the first and 25-12 Toronto in the second. The Leafs outshot the Canucks 13-6 in the middle frame. It was the third time this season Vancouver outshot an opponent overall. Six of the Canucks' last eight losses have been by two goals or fewer.

Elias Pettersson's six-game point streak ended, a run of two goals and five assists. He drew three penalties, blocked five shots, and threw three hits, but went 7-for-25 on faceoffs, 28 percent. He told Postmedia he was not too good with the puck, made too many errors, and was terrible in the faceoff dot. No NHLer has taken more faceoffs than he has this season: 337 through 16 games, at a 45 percent win rate, and he has no five-on-five goal since January. Head coach Manny Malhotra said Pettersson is frustrated on offence but is blocking shots and recovering pucks with more jam, and that the offence will come. On the loss, Malhotra said there is progress, but it is tough to see when there is no correlation to wins, and he pointed to breakouts through the neutral zone in the second. Boeser said the team is generating more shots and the defensive game is coming along. Sasson said it is tough in the room, and that the group has to stick with the process. Malhotra said every game Meriläinen has played this year he has given them an opportunity to win, and that the run of starts is because of that.

Centre Jacob Quillan, acquired October 15 in a trade from Toronto and recalled Friday from Abbotsford of the AHL, made his Canucks debut in place of Filip Chytil, who was placed on injured reserve after reaggravating a shoulder injury in Thursday's 3-2 loss at the San Jose Sharks. Malhotra said Quillan made poised plays on breakouts and had a few good forechecks, and that one game is not a full analysis. Jack Roslovic earned an assist on Matthews's goal and extended a six-game point streak to three goals and seven assists. Toronto has 28 wins in 86 games in Vancouver. Leafs coach Jim Hiller said the team has been too inconsistent, and that the second period was as good a forecheck as they have had all year. After the win, Sportsnet reported Nikita Kucherov had requested a trade from Tampa Bay amid a contract stalemate with general manager Julien BriseBois, who has said he has no intention to trade the 33-year-old. The two sides remain millions apart. Elliotte Friedman reported that Toronto and Montreal would be considered among Canadian landing spots. Darren Raddysh, a former Lightning teammate, said he wished both sides the best. Vancouver hosts the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday. Toronto hosts the Utah Mammoth on Tuesday. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12129011/matthews-nylander-lead-leafs-to-win-over-canucks/) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12129050/canucks-point-to-progress-as-losses-pile-up/) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/i-watched-this-game-ex-canucks-maple-leafs-halloween)

**B.C. Lions defeat the Saskatchewan Roughriders in CFL West semifinal: CBC British Columbia**
Nathan Rourke passed for 366 yards and the B.C. Lions came all the way back to beat the Saskatchewan Roughriders 33-26 in the CFL West Division semifinal on Saturday in Vancouver. The Edmonton Elks are set to face the B.C. Lions at Commonwealth Stadium in the Western Final. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/cfl/cfl-playoffs-saskatchewan-roughriders-bc-lions-9.7403260?cmp=rss) Source: [cfweradio.ca](https://cfweradio.ca/2026/10/31/45512/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A 5.9-billion-dollar Delta port expansion could open four years sooner under Ottawa's listing.**

**What You Need to Know:** Ottawa's national-interest listing for the $5.9-billion Roberts Bank Terminal 2 expansion in Delta could move commercial operations to 2035, four years earlier than 2039. The Supreme Court of Canada has ordered a new trial in a Vancouver crash that killed a toddler. Surrey has a new police chief, and mayor-elect Doug McCallum has slammed the appointment.

### Top Stories
**New trial ordered for driver acquitted in crash that killed Vancouver toddler: CBC British Columbia**
Canada's top court has ordered a new trial for a man acquitted of dangerous driving in a crash that killed a Vancouver toddler in 2021. CBC British Columbia reports the Supreme Court of Canada sent the case back after that acquittal. Global BC reports the man was behind the wheel, and that the crash badly injured the child's father. The ruling returns the dangerous-driving case to court. He remains a man who was acquitted, not someone a court has found guilty. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-toddler-killed-crash-new-trial-ocean-9.7402786?cmp=rss) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12127998/new-trial-ordered-man-deadly-vancouver-crash-killed-toddler/)

**Todd Matsumoto named new Surrey Police Service chief: CBC**
Todd Matsumoto is the new chief of the Surrey Police Service. CBC reports he took over as interim chief in June after the dismissal of former chief constable Norm Lipinski. The Vancouver Sun reports mayor-elect Doug McCallum has slammed the move to make that appointment permanent. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/new-surrey-police-chief-9.7403318?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/todd-matsumoto-named-permanent-surrey-police-chief)

**Delta rally attendees call for answers after Tsawwassen Mills crash: CBC British Columbia**
Rally attendees in Delta are calling for clearer answers about the deadly collision at Tsawwassen Mills. CBC British Columbia reports the community wants more concrete detail on what happened, including whether the driver experienced a medical event before the crash. That question is what attendees are asking. It is not a finding about the driver. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/delta-rally-tsawwassen-mills-crash-9.7404050?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Vaughn Palmer: Lorne Doerkson bent on getting rid of NDP's controversial housing bill: Vancouver Sun**
Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson is sticking to a vow to roll back the David Eby government's role in local decisions on housing density, single-family zoning, and related policies, Vaughn Palmer writes in the Vancouver Sun. The column describes Eby's legislation as imposing densities of up to six units on standard lots at the local level. The vow is a stated intention from the premier-designate, not a law passed today. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/vaughn-palmer-doerkson-bent-on-getting-rid-of-bill-44)

**New government will examine BC Ferries shipbuilding, Doerkson says: Global BC**
Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson says the new government will examine BC Ferries shipbuilding. Global BC reports he was speaking about a deal made last year. Doerkson said he does not know what the deal looks like, and that the government would have an interest in seeing it. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12127816/new-government-examine-bc-ferries-shipbuilding-doerkson/)

**New Vanderhoof detox centre adds 5 'badly needed' recovery beds to northern B.C.: CBC British Columbia**
Carrier Sekani Family Services is now operating a five-bed detox centre in Vanderhoof. CBC British Columbia reports the beds add recovery capacity in northern British Columbia. The agency is also preparing to open a much larger facility at nearby Tachick Lake. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vanderhoof-detox-centre-9.7401936?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**Feds list Port of Vancouver's $5.9 billion Roberts Bank Terminal 2 as project of national interest: Vancouver Sun**
The federal government has named Roberts Bank Terminal 2, the planned container expansion at the Port of Vancouver in Delta, a project of national interest. Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon announced the listing Friday, October 30, at the Delta port, with Delta MP Jill McKnight, B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson, Tsawwassen First Nation Chief Laura Cassidy, and Vancouver Fraser Port Authority president and CEO Peter Xotta beside him. The Surrey Now-Leader reports the step is meant to streamline approvals for the $5.9-billion project and to accelerate commercial operations by up to four years, to 2035 rather than 2039. Business in Vancouver reports the expansion is expected to add 2.4 million containers of capacity. The Vancouver Sun reports this is the second project fast-tracked by Prime Minister Mark Carney's major projects office.

MacKinnon called the Port of Vancouver Canada's largest by a long margin. He said it connects Canadian businesses to more than 170 markets and handles about one-third of Canada's trade outside the United States. He tied the expansion to a federal goal of doubling exports to non-U.S. markets by 2035, and said an investment in the port is an investment in farmers, manufacturers, producers, exporters, small businesses, and communities across the country. Carney said in a statement that the listing better connects the economy with the world and diversifies trade, and that Canada will not wait as the world competes for capital. The Surrey Now-Leader reports the designation lets the project bypass remaining federal permits and authorizations. The Major Projects Office will keep coordinating consultation with Indigenous communities, and a conditions document will be issued by the minister responsible under the act, currently Internal Trade Minister Dominic Leblanc. Senior government officials told a technical briefing that document can be ready within a couple of months. Environmental protections are among the conditions, including effects on southern resident killer whales, described as an endangered species, and on chinook salmon. The port authority has proposed avoidance, mitigation, and offsetting, including measures for underwater noise, and has committed to 102 hectares of fish-habitat offsetting.

Chief Laura Cassidy said Tsawwassen First Nation's support is not unconditional. She said the nation still has concerns about the long-term health of the Fraser River estuary and the Salish Sea, and that years of consultation produced accommodations for Tsawwassen harvesters, environmental measures, and commitments to ongoing oversight. She said the nation sought assurances the Building Canada Act would not be used to cut corners or weaken protections, and that Canada committed to upholding conditions the nation has long fought for and to managing impacts in the spirit of their treaty. Cassidy said a high priority is a breach in the Roberts Bank Causeway to improve habitat access for young salmon, and that major projects should aim for net environmental gain rather than only minimizing harm. # Vancouver Daily News
> **Sixteen years and eight months is the sentence for the Surrey bus attack.**

**What You Need to Know:** Sixteen years and eight months is the sentence for the Surrey bus attack, after a 2025 conviction for attempted murder and aggravated assault. Vancouver has named a new fire chief to start Monday. A jury has again found Alvaro Julio Roche-Garcia guilty of first-degree murder in a 2019 porch shooting.

### Top Stories
**Man sentenced to 16 years, 8 months for horrifying Surrey bus attack: Global BC**
Abdul Aziz Kawam was convicted in 2025 in the 2023 Islamic State knife attack on a B.C. bus and sentenced to 15 years for attempted murder and 20 months for aggravated assault. He will serve 16 years and 8 months in prison, CBC reports. Global News reports that on April 1, 2023, security video showed Abdul Kawam walking onto the bus, followed a few seconds later by his victim. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-sentencing-2023-islamic-state-knife-attack-on-b-c-bus-9.7402210?cmp=rss) Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12126271/man-sentenced-16-years-8-months-horrifying-surrey-bus-attack/)

**Vancouver man found guilty of first-degree murder for a 2nd time: Global BC**
A jury has found Alvaro Julio Roche-Garcia guilty of first-degree murder for a second time in the January 2019 shooting of 69-year-old Zenen Cepeda Silva, who was gunned down on a porch on Fraser Street in Vancouver while sitting with his wife. Roche-Garcia was arrested shortly after. Silva’s wife suffered a stroke before the first trial and never took the stand; the jury in that trial heard an audio recording from a preliminary inquiry in which she said her husband’s dying words were “look how Alvaro has killed me.” B.C.’s highest court found the trial judge erred by allowing the jury to treat that alleged declaration as fact when the testimony was never cross-examined, struck the conviction in 2024, and ordered a new trial. After five weeks, the new jury returned a guilty verdict; Global News reports a motive was never made clear. Crown counsel Daniel Port said the couple knew the accused for about 15 years in Albuquerque, New Mexico, and Vancouver; Roche-Garcia told the court he had no reason to shoot Silva, and his lawyer argued there was a lack of hard evidence linking him to the crime. A sentencing hearing is set for next month. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12126264/vancouver-man-guilty-first-degree-murder-2nd-time/)

### City & Province
**SURREY SCHOOLS Surrey Schools shares updated Accessibility Plan: Education News Canada**
With the first three years of its Accessibility Plan complete, Surrey Schools has released an updated plan for 2026-2028. The first plan launched in September 2023 for 2023-2026, under the Accessible British Columbia Regulation, which required public organizations to establish accessibility committees, plans and public-feedback mechanisms as of September 2023. Assistant Superintendent Shauna Ross and District Principal Colin Reid presented the new plan at the October Surrey Board of Education meeting. Reid said a district-wide assessment of parking lots, entrances, doors, learning commons and emergency preparedness across all sites has informed recent renovations and new-building decisions, and that an animated accessibility video series has been viewed thousands of times and used by municipalities, non-profits, advocacy groups and other B.C. school districts. Looking ahead, the district’s priorities include annual site assessments, an accessibility space on each site’s website, National AccessAbility Week shaped by student input, and tactile wayfinding signage at three sites: DEC, REC and Sunnyside Elementary. Reid said the work has stayed with the statement “Nothing About Us, Without Us.” Source: [educationnewscanada.com](https://educationnewscanada.com/article/education/level/k12/3/1225761/surrey-schools-shares-updated-accessibility-plan.html)

**SURREY SCHOOLS Surrey teacher wins national award for forest-based kindergarten program: Education News Canada**
Ellen Petersson, a kindergarten teacher at Ray Sheperd Elementary in South Surrey, has received the Susan Langley Earth Steward Teaching Award, a national honour from Learning for a Sustainable Future. For six years her students have spent part of every school day in the forest beside the school, rain or shine. They practise math with pinecones, make art with leaves, and study science by watching insects, the weather and the seasons. Petersson said five-year-olds may not yet understand climate change, biodiversity loss or sustainability as adults do, but they understand wonder, curiosity and caring for a place they love. In 2020 a local senior the class calls Grandfriend Don began joining the outdoor lessons, and grandparents, retirees, parents and community elders followed. She brings in the principle of reciprocity — bird feeders in winter, bug hotels in the fall, keeping natural spaces clean — and said, “We need the children to love the earth before we ask them to save it.” Source: [educationnewscanada.com](https://educationnewscanada.com/article/education/level/k12/3/1225763/surrey-teacher-wins-national-award-for-forest-based-kindergarten-program.html)

### The Closer Look
**City of Richmond moves to acquire Watermania aquatic centre through expropriation ahead of lease expiry: Daily Hive Vancouver**
The City of Richmond is moving to take ownership of Watermania by expropriation as the long-term lease nears its expiry in March 2027. Daily Hive reports a formal expropriation notice dated July 3, 2026, was filed with the Land Title Office on July 6. It identifies 14300 Entertainment Blvd. Investments as the registered owner. Watermania sits at the Riverport Sports and Entertainment Complex in southeast Richmond, beside Silver City Riverport Cinemas, Splitsville Bowl Riverport and Richmond Ice Centre. The City operates the centre as a public recreation facility but does not own the building or the land; both have been leased from a private landowner since the centre was completed nearly 30 years ago. The notice says acquiring the property would serve the public interest by ensuring Watermania continues providing essential community services as a public indoor aquatic centre and fitness facility, and by supporting long-term financial and asset management through a fee-simple interest. Services could be provided by Richmond or by another public authority, person or organization acting on its behalf. The notice does not set out a purchase price or compensation offer. The private landowner has initiated a formal independent inquiry, scheduled to begin in late November 2026. Outgoing Mayor Malcom Brodie told Daily Hive that expropriation is used very infrequently and avoided whenever possible, that Watermania is an important recreation facility, and that the City’s goal is to secure its long-term future. He said that because the matter is before an independent inquiry, it would not be appropriate to comment further, and that the City respects the process and looks forward to a fair outcome.

The lease arrangement dates to the 1990s. Richmond voters approved borrowing about $20 million in a 1993 referendum to build a publicly owned aquatic centre on City-owned land. Council later cancelled that capital project because it wanted to avoid additional debt, and selected a proposal from the Riverport developer, which financed construction and leased the centre to the City. Watermania opened in 1997. BC Assessment’s latest roll values it at $49.4 million — $27.41 million for the land and $21.99 million for the building — as estimated market value as of July 1, 2025. In 2019 the City bought the adjacent Richmond Ice Centre, also privately developed and leased for public recreation, when that lease came up for renewal. The City said money previously spent on annual lease payments there would help fund renovations. Richmond Olympic Oval, by contrast, was built as a City-owned facility for the 2010 Winter Olympics. The City operates four public swimming facilities: year-round indoor swimming at Watermania and Minoru Centre for Active Living, and seasonal outdoor pools at South Arm and Steveston.

The people most directly affected are Richmond residents who use the indoor wave pool, two long waterslides and the 57-metre competition pool with a movable bulkhead, plus the fitness centre, diving boards and tower, whirlpools, steam room and sauna. Brodie’s stated case is that ownership secures that public use for the long term. The landowner’s response now on the record is the independent inquiry set for late November 2026. Daily Hive also notes a separate uncertainty over value: in August 2025, B.C. Supreme Court Justice Barbara Young granted the Cowichan Tribes Aboriginal title over about 740 acres of public and private land north and east of Riverport. The City of Richmond, the federal and provincial governments, Musqueam First Nation and Tsawwassen First Nation have appealed. The Cowichan Tribes have filed their own appeal seeking title over the full 1,846 acres of the original claim, and a City map shows that broader area includes the Riverport complex. Those appeals could run for years. The next dated step the source names for the pool itself is the inquiry in late November 2026. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/watermania-aquatic-centre-city-of-richmond-expropriation-acquisition)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A century of clock changes ends in B.C., leaving morning commutes darker.**

**What You Need to Know:** For the first time in more than a century, British Columbia will not turn the clocks back this fall, and Vancouver Coastal Health warns the morning commute will be darker than usual. The B.C. NDP caucus meets at the legislature today to pick an interim leader after falling from 47 seats to 28. Federal Liberals voted Wednesday to keep the north-coast oil tanker ban.

### Top Stories
**As B.C. scraps time change, experts have a warning about the risks: Global BC**
For the first time in more than a century, B.C. will not turn the clocks back this fall. Vancouver Coastal Health warns the morning commute will be darker than usual and could discourage walking or biking to school or work. The health authority recommends bright colours, reflective gear and eye contact with drivers, and tells drivers to slow down for the conditions. Ralph Mistlberger, a psychology professor at Simon Fraser University, told Global News that humans depend on morning light to set the body’s internal clock, and that later morning light makes it easier to stay up and harder to wake while a fixed social schedule does not move. He co-authored a Canadian Medical Association Journal report on the dangers of year-round daylight time. Patrick Baylis of the University of British Columbia’s School of Economics said the change hits harder when work hours are less flexible and a start time sits near the old sunrise, including a required 8 a.m. start. After November 1, B.C. will be one hour ahead of Washington State. Alberta and Manitoba are also ending the clock change this year. Quebec’s government said Wednesday it plans to scrap the change. Saskatchewan has not changed its clocks since 1966, and Yukon ended the practice in 2020. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12125021/bc-time-change-experts-warn/)

**Decimated B.C. NDP caucus meeting to discuss interim leadership after election loss: Global BC**
Members of the B.C. NDP caucus meet at the legislature Thursday to discuss who will be interim leader after the weekend election defeat. The caucus is down to 28 members after entering Saturday’s election with 47, while the B.C. Conservatives hold 63 seats. Outgoing Premier David Eby announced his resignation as party leader in his election-night concession speech, and it is not clear if he will attend. The outgoing caucus met online on Wednesday. MLA-elect Niki Sharma is expected to speak to reporters ahead of this morning’s meeting. Geoff Meggs, chief of staff to the late former NDP premier John Horgan, said Wednesday that the next leader faces the reputational challenge of proving the party can be trusted with taxpayers’ money, and that voters want services protected and some balance in spending. Horgan left a $5.7-billion surplus when he stepped aside in 2022. The deficit is forecast to hit $14 billion this year. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12125620/bc-ndp-election-meeting/)

**B.C. North Coast tanker ban to remain in place after Liberals vote down Tory bill: CBC British Columbia**
The federal Liberal government voted Wednesday to keep the B.C. coastal oil tanker ban in place, defeating a Conservative bill that would have repealed it. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/bc-north-coast-tanker-ban-vote-9.7400350?cmp=rss)

**'Blessing scams' in Vancouver switch gold, cash for noodles, water bottles: VPD: CBC British Columbia**
Vancouver police say blessing scams have targeted seniors at bus stops. One woman handed over valuables worth $90,000 and received a backpack of noodles and water bottles. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-blessing-scams-police-warn-9.7399512?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**‘Indestructible’ Downtown Eastside toilet suddenly out of service: Global BC**
The City of Vancouver’s Portland Loo at Main and Powell, which opened June 8, is closed for a lock repair less than five months later. Procurement and installation cost $446,145, and annual maintenance is about $95,000. The city said the repair is a lock part or a replacement lock system, that it does not expect a large cost, and that the bill may fall inside the maintenance budget or need extra funding. Six Portland Loos are in Vancouver. The Park Board manages five: two in CRAB Park, two in Columbia Park and one in Coopers’ Park. The city manages the Main and Powell unit. Community member Nat Canuel said a previous self-cleaning toilet there sat broken for years, and that this one, bought in time for the World Cup, lasted four months. People in the neighbourhood say someone had been living in the washroom for about a week before a closed-for-repairs sign appeared. The Park Board had billed the units as almost indestructible. The two in CRAB Park survived more than two years of an encampment. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12124727/indestructible-downtown-eastside-toilet-suddenly-out-of-service/)

**Accessibility in Action: The District's Plan: Education News Canada**
The Burnaby School District has a renewed Accessibility Plan for 2026 to 2029, after a first plan in 2023 under the Accessible British Columbia Act. Superintendent Karim Hachlaf introduced it at the board’s last public meeting and said it reflects consultation with students, staff, families, community partners and people with lived experience of disability. The three priorities are understanding accessibility together, accessible learning and working environments, and inclusive employment and organizational practices. Director of Instruction Kelly Chow told the board accessibility is an ongoing journey and that the plan is a framework for the next three years, not the end of the work. Source: [educationnewscanada.com](https://educationnewscanada.com/article/education/level/k12/3/1225728/accessibility-in-action-the-district-s-plan.html)

**The winner of this B.C. school trustee race was decided by random draw: Vancouver Sun**
Incumbent Shelley Sim was declared winner of a Kamloops-Thompson school district trustee seat after a judicial recount tied her with Lee Onslow, 337 to 337, and a random draw broke the tie. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/school-trustee-candidates-kamloops-tied)

**Vancouver teacher suspended for breaching ‘position of power and trust’ with Grade 7 student: CBC British Columbia**

Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-teacher-suspended-crush-inappropriate-conduct-9.7398893?cmp=rss)

### The Closer Look
**Maple Green's Penny Hill honoured with Dyslexia Canada award: Education News Canada**
Penny Hill, learning support teacher at Maple Green Elementary in Surrey, received a Dyslexia Canada Educational Excellence Award at a school assembly on October 6. Alicia Smith, executive director of Dyslexia Canada, travelled from Ottawa to present it. Angie Calleberg, executive director of curriculum and assessment at the Ministry of Education and Child Care, shared a message of congratulations. The award recognizes educators who advance structured literacy instruction, universal screening and effective intervention, and who support colleagues through leadership and knowledge-sharing.

Hill’s path started in her first year of teaching, when some students responded to her instruction and others did not. In 2003 she attended a workshop in California and learned about dyslexia. “I remember crying,” she said. “I thought to myself, ‘I can help these kids.’” She began tutoring and brought that approach into class, teaching every student as if they were dyslexic, with a focus on what she calls metaphonological awareness. That conclusion became the thesis of her master’s degree in special education, completed under Dr. Linda Siegel, an authority on learning disabilities. Explicit, systematic, evidence-based instruction is “helpful for all, harmful for none and crucial for some,” Hill said.

Screening for early reading difficulties began at Maple Green when Hill joined. Staff screen students with Acadience and DIBELS. She shared the work with colleagues. Former principal Jennifer Pilchak encouraged lunch-and-learn sessions. Hill joked that the encouragement was free lunch. She has presented at conventions in Canada and abroad, guest lectured in university special education classes, led lunch-and-learns, and now mentors a cohort of learning support teachers. Principal Michael Speak said, “This award is so well deserved. Penny has spent her career making sure students with dyslexia are seen, understood and taught in ways that work for them. We are incredibly proud to have her at Maple Green.”

Hill said she has been knocking on the doors of people who control policy for decades. She said she is encouraged that many more people want to know about dyslexia and how to ameliorate its effects. The award names a Surrey teacher whose screening, classroom method and mentoring already shape how colleagues at Maple Green, and the learning support teachers she mentors, teach early reading. Source: [educationnewscanada.com](https://educationnewscanada.com/article/education/level/k12/3/1225767/maple-green-s-penny-hill-honoured-with-dyslexia-canada-award.html)

> **Nine hundred fourteen dollars is what the average home would pay Metro Vancouver if Friday's budget vote holds.**

### The Closer Look
**Dan Fumano: In poignant final council meeting, Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim and most of his party say goodbye and good luck: Vancouver Sun**
Ken Sim presided Tuesday over his last Vancouver city council meeting, the only public session between the October 17 election that defeated him and ABC and the November 2 swearing-in of the new council.

Partway through, he dropped the titles he had used for four years. Instead of Coun. Kirby-Yung, Coun. Dominato and Coun. Fry, he said Sarah, Lisa and Pete. Vancouver Sun columnist Dan Fumano wrote that the change did not read as disrespect, but as warmth toward colleagues his party had campaigned against, sometimes aggressively.

The term opened on a different note. After ABC's 2022 landslide, Sim's party gave some board roles to councillors from outside the team and talked about being post-partisan. By the halfway point, Sim had stripped non-ABC councillors of those extra roles and the pay that came with them. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, politicians elected with ABC resigned from caucus or were ejected after splits over abolishing the elected park board, halting the municipal ethics watchdog's work, and freezing supportive housing construction.

When the campaign began in September, Sim was party to two defamation lawsuits that are still going. He is the plaintiff suing former chief of staff Kareem Allam, who ran against him for mayor. He is a defendant in a suit filed by Coun. Sean Orr.

Before Tuesday's meeting, Sim embraced Orr, who was re-elected with three new councillors from COPE. Asked about that chat, Sim said, "You know, bygones be bygones," and that Orr had stepped up to serve even where their politics differ.

Outgoing councillors then addressed the room. ABC's Lisa Dominato, Sarah Kirby-Yung, Lenny Zhou and Peter Meiszner, all defeated for a second term, and Rebecca Bligh, elected with ABC in 2022 and a mayoral candidate this year against Sim, thanked staff and voters and wished their successors well. Brian Montague, who did not seek re-election, attended and did not speak.

Sim spoke last. He thanked his family, joked, and paraphrased Dickens to his colleagues: it had been the best of times, and sometimes not the best of times, and he was not going to say the worst of times. He said that on his deathbed he would look back on being mayor as the most meaningful thing he had been involved in. The new council is sworn in November 2. Fumano's column notes that Pete Fry, who unseated Sim, will be Vancouver's first Green mayor. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/opinion/columnists/vancouver-mayor-ken-sim-abc-party-final-council-meeting) Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/player/play/video/9.7399054)

### Both Sides: Metro Vancouver's Friday budget vote
Friday, Metro Vancouver's board meets to work through a 1,190-page agenda and to approve the 2027 budget and five-year financial plan. The board is mayors and councillors from 21 municipalities, each with a weighted vote by the size of their city. The proposed budget calls for nearly $1.7 billion in operating spending, a 7.4 per cent increase from this year, and $2 billion in planned capital spending. The average household's bill for regional water, sewer, garbage and parks is projected to rise to $914 a year from $897.

Surrey mayor-elect Doug McCallum says Friday's October 30 meeting should be cancelled until the new mayors are sworn in. He says that on October 17, voters in 13 of the region's 21 municipalities chose a new mayor, including Vancouver, Surrey, Richmond, Coquitlam, Delta and both Langleys, and that an outgoing board should not set what every household pays. His strongest reason is time and accountability: the board has until next March to adopt its financial plan, so waiting for the November 27 regular meeting should not be a problem. If one item truly cannot wait four weeks, he says, deal with that item and leave the rest. He has asked board chair Mike Hurley and the directors to cancel.

New Westminster mayor-elect Daniel Fontaine says he fully supports that request. He says about two-thirds of the 41 directors were defeated, resigned or did not run again, and that ratifying a significant budget in the dying days of this board is incomprehensible. His case is that people who will not face the voters for these decisions should not lock in a plan the next board may have to manage for four years. He says Metro Vancouver is not under a statutory deadline to approve the budget Friday. He also plans to push an accountability charter, already backed by West Vancouver's mayor-elect Kirk LaPointe and White Rock's mayor-elect Chris Shields, including a full review of cost overruns at the North Shore wastewater treatment plant.

A Metro Vancouver spokesperson said Monday the 2027 budget will be considered and voted on this Friday. The reason given is practical: an October decision gives member jurisdictions time to prepare their own financial plans and to meet legislative requirements for when budgets should be established. The spokesperson said board meetings fall on the last Friday of every month regardless of the election cycle. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/metro-vancouver-rejects-surrey-doug-mccallum-cancel-meeting)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **BC Ferries removes CEO Nicolas Jimenez and launches a review of service and demand.**

**What You Need to Know:** BC Ferries has removed chief executive Nicolas Jimenez and launched a review of service and demand. Brian Anderson, vice-president of strategy and planning, is interim CEO effective immediately, while chief financial officer Dallyn Willis leads that review and a permanent search follows it. Jimenez took the job in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he worked with then-Attorney General David Eby on no-fault insurance.

### Top Stories
**Nicolas Jimenez out as B.C. Ferries CEO, review launched: CBC British Columbia**
Nicolas Jimenez is out as chief executive of BC Ferries, and the board has launched a review. Daily Hive reported the departure as sudden. Brian Anderson, vice-president of strategy and planning, is interim CEO effective immediately. Executive vice-president and chief financial officer Dallyn Willis will lead a review aimed at improving service and meeting growing demand, with the board overseeing it. A formal search for a permanent CEO follows that review. Jimenez took over in 2023 after leaving ICBC, where he had worked closely with then-Attorney General David Eby on the transition to no-fault insurance. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/nicolas-jimenez-out-as-b-c-ferries-ceo-review-launched-9.7396867?cmp=rss) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/hullo-ferries-new-ceo-louisa-bell)

**B.C. election sets record for lowest voter turnout: Global BC**
Elections BC’s preliminary figures show 48 percent of eligible voters cast a ballot, fewer than half, and about 10 percentage points below the 2024 provincial election. Stewart Prest, a political science lecturer at UBC, told Global News, “This is Mr. Eby’s low-turnout election to own, and this is going to be part of his legacy.” The NDP received more than 270,000 fewer votes than in 2024. The Conservatives received about 49,000 fewer. Prest said the early call looked politically opportunistic to some previous NDP supporters, and that the party did not present a positive vision on housing affordability and jobs. He said some Conservative voters, asked back to the polls two years after the last election, were motivated to send the governing party a message. Prest said people are more likely to vote when they believe the vote matters and when governments deliver on housing and jobs. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12120927/bc-election-record-lowest-voter-turnout/)

**Victoria backs amalgamation, but Saanich voters reject becoming a single larger city with B.C.'s capital: Daily Hive Vancouver**
Saanich voters rejected becoming one municipality with Victoria, so the non-binding idea does not have the yes from both communities that Saanich said was required before any further work. In Saanich, 24,663 votes, 68 percent, were against, and 11,626, 32 percent, were in favour. In Victoria, 17,523 votes, 62 percent, were in favour, and 10,890, 38 percent, were against, among 28,413 responses. Both municipalities asked the same question on October 17, 2026: “Do you support Saanich and Victoria becoming one municipality?” Saanich had said a no in either community meant no further amalgamation work. The outgoing BC NDP government had said that even a yes in both places would not merge them: more information on costs, transition and services, plus consultation with area First Nations, would be needed before a binding referendum could be considered. In 2018, voters in both communities supported funding a citizens’ assembly. That assembly of 48 randomly selected residents recommended a merger in 2025, and its final report was presented that July. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/victoria-saanich-october-2026-amalgamation-plebiscite-election-results)

**Uniqlo to move into old Nordstrom building in downtown Vancouver: Global BC**
Uniqlo said it will open a flagship in the former Nordstrom building at Pacific Centre early next year, in the same year as the tenth anniversary of its first B.C. store, at Metrotown in Burnaby. Nordstrom closed in 2023. Last year the 230,000-square-foot space was slated to be split into four units. Simons and Aritzia are taking two of those quadrants. After Uniqlo takes the third, one unit remains vacant. Nordstrom had been there since 2015. Eaton’s and Sears had left the same location before that. Aritzia said its store will span four levels and include a dining concept it described as casual yet elevated. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12121819/uniqlo-move-nordstrom-building-downtown-vancouver/)

### The Closer Look
**Vancouver International Airport records its busiest month ever with over 2.8 million passengers: Daily Hive Vancouver**
August 2026 was the first month in Vancouver International Airport’s history to reach and pass 2.8 million passengers, arrivals and departures combined. Daily Hive, using YVR’s latest official statistics, put the August total at 2.815 million. That beat July 2026, itself a record at 2.73 million, by about 83,000 passengers. Before this summer, the busiest month had been August 2018, at 2.71 million.

Compared with August 2025, when YVR recorded 2.65 million passengers, August 2026 was higher by about 168,000, or 6.3 percent. July and August together brought nearly 5.55 million passengers through the airport. WestJet labour disruptions in late July and early August affected both months. August alone averaged about 90,800 passengers a day. September’s final figures are due next month.

Domestic flights were the largest share of August traffic and a large part of the increase in raw numbers, from 1.33 million in August 2025 to 1.45 million, almost 119,000 more passengers, or 8.9 percent. International volumes outside the United States reached over 727,000, up 12.7 percent from about 645,000 in August 2025. Within that, Asia-Pacific routes accounted for about 441,000 passengers, up 18.6 percent. YVR has told Daily Hive it has seen a resurgence in volumes from Mainland China since last year, which it links to the strength of that market. European routes recorded another 240,000 passengers, up 5.2 percent from the same month in 2025.

U.S. transborder volumes moved the other way. They fell to about 635,000 in August 2026, from 668,000 in August 2025, a decline of more than 33,000 passengers, or about five percent. In August 2024, before the re-election of U.S. president Donald Trump, YVR saw 700,000 passengers on U.S. routes. For well over a year, some airlines have reduced frequencies or suspended Canada-U.S. routes and shifted capacity to other domestic and international flying. Air Canada confirmed last week that two seasonal routes linking YVR with Nashville and Raleigh will not return for summer 2027 as previously scheduled.

July’s volumes were driven in part by visitation for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Growth in July and August was also supported by tourism demand, including a cruise season that brought 1.4 million passengers through the Canada Place terminal. August is typically one of YVR’s busiest months, with summer trips and students heading back for school. Over the first eight months of 2026, YVR recorded 18.92 million passengers, up 4.1 percent from 18.18 million in the same stretch of 2025, and the highest January-to-August total the airport has recorded. The full-year record is 26.9 million passengers in 2025. Daily Hive noted that if the rest of 2026 holds this pace, the annual total could exceed that mark. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/vancouver-international-airport-yvr-summer-2026-passenger-statistics-record)

The Saskatchewan Roughriders play the B.C. Lions on Saturday at B.C. Place, a building where they lost twice this season, including 30-16 on August 23. ### Both Sides: Repealing DRIPA
The B.C. Conservative government-elect says it will repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act. The Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs says the law should stay and be used, not torn up. The act passed unanimously in the legislature in 2019. Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said the day after the election that his party is committed to repealing it.

Doerkson’s case is that the law has not solved the conflicts it was meant to settle. He said, “The reality is it hasn’t solved anything.” He pointed to court fights over docks at Pender Harbour and over mining opportunities, and said the province needs to “work together for the betterment of all people in British Columbia.”

Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, president of the Union of British Columbia Indian Chiefs, calls DRIPA the roadmap to reconciliation and the way to recognize inherent title and rights. He said the chiefs will not stand idly by if the government-elect rips it up, and he called that “a declaration of war.” He framed the choice as whether British Columbia becomes “a war zone” or keeps doing “the challenging work of reconciliation.” The Union of B.C. Indian Chiefs urges the new government to use the act as the framework for that work rather than repeal it.

Doerkson said his party is contemplating a shortened fall session, so the repeal is not likely to reach the legislature until spring. First Nations groups are already stating the consequences they see if it does. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12121663/bc-first-nations-chief-warns-ripping-dripa-declaration-war/)
